Their tails are heavy at the base, set high and carried over the back with the end falling on the body.
These dogs have a medium sized muzzle, neither pointed nor square, but should be proportionate to its skull.
Lhasa Apsos have a variety of coat colors, including cream, gold, honey, slate, black, white, and parti-color.
Flat-Coated Retriever: These dogs are medium to large-sized breeds, taller and more racily built than Labradors.
They are known for their flat-lying, dense, and glossy black or liver coats, which help protect them in cold water.
Their heads are distinctive, being long and of unique 'one-piece' construction without a pronounced stop, or angle between the forehead and the muzzle.
They are famous for their bright and cheerful expression, which is characterized by their almond-shaped, dark brown eyes and feathered ears that hang close to the head.
They have a strong, muscular build with a deep chest and well-developed hindquarters.
These dogs possess a powerful, smooth gait, reflecting their heritage as an efficient game retriever.
Flat-Coated Retrievers have a long tail which is generally carried straight or slightly raised, but not curled or overly extended over the back.
Curly-coated Retriever: They are known for their distinctive water-resistant, curly coat, which is black or liver in color.
The dog is a large breed, they have a robust and agile body suitable for all types of terrain.
In terms of size comparison, they can stand taller or as tall as a common kitchen table.
They have a wedge-shaped head with almond-shaped eyes that are either brown or black, complimenting the coat color.
Their ears are small and lie close to their head.
The tail of the Curly-coated Retriever is straight and hangs down.
They are characterized by their friendly and confident disposition, often portrayed with a cheerful and playful body language.
Golden Retriever: Golden Retrievers are well-known for their beautiful, dense, water-repellent coat which has a top coat that is water-resistant and slightly wavy, and a thick undercoat.
Coat color ranges from light golden to dark golden and they have a thick and beautiful fur.
Golden Retrievers are medium to large sized dogs, typically weighing between 55 and 75 pounds.
They have a robust, muscular body with a broad head, wide-set eyes and large, dropping ears.
Golden Retrievers have a friendly and tolerant attitude. They are outgoing, trustworthy, and eager to please.
They have a strong, broad, and deep body with a straight back and a well-groomed tail that is carried level with the back.
The relative size of Golden Retrievers is larger compared to other objects in the image.
Labrador Retriever: Labrador Retrievers are commonly seen in three colors: black, chocolate (brown), and yellow.
Labrador Retrievers are often characterized by their short, dense, weather resistant coat, which is relatively straight and smooth to the touch.
The breed is known for its broad skull and strongly pronounced brow ridge, giving it a friendly and intelligent look.
Labrador Retrievers have medium-sized eyes that are usually brown or hazel in color and are set well apart in their heads.
This breed features ears that hang down close to their heads, set somewhat far back, and are not overly large or heavy.
Labradors are large and strong dogs with a solid build and are usually medium to large in size in comparison to other objects or beings in the photo.
The breed has a distinctive 'otter tail' that is very thick at the base, medium length, and tapers towards the tip.
Chesapeake Bay Retriever: They are medium to large-sized dogs, generally weighing between 55 to 80 pounds.
They have a dense and wavy double coat which is oily and water-resistant. Their coat colors can vary from dark brown to a light tan or sedge.
Their eyes are generally amber-colored and they have a stern expression.
They have a broad skull, pronounced stop, and strong jaws.
Their ears are medium-sized, hanging, and positioned rather high on their head.
They have muscular, powerful bodies with webbed toes which aid them in swimming.
They have a deep chest and strong hindquarters, suitable for untiring work.
German Shorthaired Pointer: This breed is typically medium to large size, with males typically weighing between 55 and 70 pounds, and females between 45 and 60 pounds.
It is known for a distinctive coat that is liver (a rich brown color), or liver and white in various patterns such as ticked, patched, or roan.
It has a strong, powerful, and agile body that allows it to move quickly and turn easily, making it a versatile hunting dog.
It has a long, broad, and strong muzzle with a powerful scissor-like bite. The nose is usually brown to match the coat.
Its eyes are medium-sized, almond-shaped, and dark brown, with an intelligent and energetic expression.
It has long and floppy ears that sit high on its head and hang down to the jawline.
The tail is typically docked at a young age to around 40% of its natural length.
Vizsla: Vizslas are medium-sized dogs, typically weighing between 45 to 60 pounds and standing about 21 to 24 inches tall.
The Vizsla has a sleek, muscular body that demonstrates their athleticism and ability to work as a hunter dog.
They are known for their distinct reddish coat that blends between golden rust and a dark sandy color.
Vizslas have a noble, slightly domed head with a tapered muzzle, and their eyes and nose usually match the color of their coat.
They have long, silky ears that hang down and frame their face.
Their tail is usually docked to two-thirds of its original length and carried horizontally.
Vizslas are characterized by a light, graceful gait that showcases their agility and power.
English Setter: This breed is characterized by a medium-sized body with a strong and elegant form.
They are recognized for their unique coat that is long and slightly wavy, which is predominantly white with interspersed patches of black, grey or tan. This is also known as a 'belton' coat.
Their ears are set well back and low, even with or below the level of the eyes. The ears are long with a rounded tip, and covered with long silky hair.
English Setters typically have a gentle expression with large, round, expressive eyes. Their eye color typically matches their coat marking color.
Despite their hunting origins, they are known for their relaxed and friendly demeanor.
The tail is quite long, set on a line with the back, or below, and tapers to a fine point. It is carried straight out or down.
English Setters are tall dogs with an elegant gait. They tend to be taller and have a less chunky build than other setter breeds.
Irish Setter: Irish Setters are known for their rich, chestnut red or mahogany coats.
This dog breed is characterized by a feathered tail that often wags in motion.
They are medium-to-large sized dogs, with males standing 27 inches tall at the shoulder and females typically a bit smaller.
They have long ears that hang down and frame their face.
Irish Setters have a distinctive slim, athletic build suitable for their history as a gundog.
They possess a friendly and intelligent expression in their almond-shaped, dark hazel eyes.
The breed has a long and elegant head with a pronounced occiput and moderate stop.
Gordon Setter: Gordon Setters are known for their glossy black coats with distinctive rich tan markings.
The Gordon Setter is a large breed, standing 23 to 27 inches tall at the shoulder and weighing between 45 and 80 pounds.
Gordon Setters have a strong, muscular frame with a deep chest and well-sprung ribs.
These dogs have a distinctive noble and intelligent expression, highlighted by their dark, oval eyes.
Their ears are set low, hanging close to the head, and they have a straight or slightly concave long snout.
They are distinctive for their robust physique and elegantly square outline, signifying strength, endurance and speed.
Gordon Setters are energetic animals, hence, they may often be seen in motion, exploring their environment.
Brittany dog: Brittanys are medium-sized dogs, known for their energetic and agile nature which is showcased in their stance and posture in images.
Brittanys have a dense coat that can come in various combinations of white and orange or liver. The coat might contain spots or be clear in color.
They usually have a medium length tail or they could be born tailless, which can be a defining attribute in photos.
Brittanys have a wedge-shaped head with a moderate stop, and their expressions usually come off as intelligent and alert.
Their eyes are typically set well in, protected by a strong brow. Eye color usually ranges from amber to hazel, depending on the coat color.
They have ears which are set high and can either lay flat or hang slightly, giving them a distinctive look.
Brittanys are strong and muscular in their build, with square or slightly longer than square physique.
Clumber Spaniel: They are recognized by their dense and heavy bone structure, giving them a look of great power and stamina.
They have a broad chest, soft and expressive eyes often in amber or dark brown color.
They have large, heavy ears set low on the sides of their heads and overlapping their cheeks.
Their coat is dense, weather-resistant, straight and flat with feathering on their ears, belly and legs. It's primarily white, with either lemon or orange markings.
They have a long body and a low stature coupled with a massive head featuring a deep, well-developed muzzle.
Relative proportions of a Clumber Spaniel usually reveal them as longer compared to their height.
The tail of a Clumber Spaniel is normally docked, with the remaining part often carried level with the back.
English Springer Spaniel: They are medium-sized dogs with compact bodies and docked tails.
They have a coat of medium length that can be black or liver with white, blue or liver roan, and tricolor, which is black and white or liver and white with tan markings.
Their coat is usually straight and glossy, with feathering on their ears, chest, belly, and the back of their legs.
They have medium-sized ears that are set high on their heads and hang down next to their cheeks.
They have a friendly and outgoing personality and are known to be eager to please.
Their eyes are typically hazel or brown, which gives them a friendly and gentle look.
They are known for their agility and their quick, brisk movements.
Welsh Springer Spaniel: Welsh Springer Spaniels are medium-sized dogs, with males standing around 18-19 inches at the shoulder and females about an inch shorter.
They have a distinctively white and red coat, with the red ranging from a deep, rich color to a lighter strawberry blond.
They have moderately long fur, with feathering on their ears, chest, belly, legs, and tail to protect them in rough and thorny hunting terrains.
Their ears are fairly large, and set at eye level. They hang close to the cheeks and are covered with silky hair.
Welsh Springer Spaniels have round, medium-sized eyes which are either hazel or dark in hue, expressing their friendly and trusting nature.
They have a sturdy and muscular build, with a slightly sloped topline from the highest point of the shoulders to the root of the tail.
The tail of this breed is usually docked and is covered with feathering that waves when in motion.
Cocker Spaniel: This breed is medium in size and has a compact, well-balanced sturdy build with a sturdy and refined appearance.
They have a distinctly rounded head with a broad and square-looking jaw. Their eyes are round, full, and slightly almond-shaped, usually dark in color.
They have long and lobular ears set at eye level. These ears are covered with long silky fur that can go beyond the length of the ear itself.
The breed is known for its beautiful smooth or wavy coat that is very dense and silky. Coat colors vary greatly including solids of black or cream, and parti-colors such as white with black or tan.
Their tails are usually docked but when undocked, it is set slightly below the line of the back with a characteristic 'merry' action, particularly when the dog is in motion.
They have a deep but not overly broad chest which is followed by well-rounded ribs.
These dogs have strong and durable legs with compact, large round feet.
Sussex Spaniel: Sussex Spaniels are known for their long, low, rectangular body shape, distinct from other spaniel breeds.
Sussex Spaniels have a unique liver-colored, wavy coat which sets them apart from the rest.
Sussex Spaniels have a deep chest and heavy-set body, which is usually wider and more substantial than in other spaniels.
Sussex Spaniels have a characteristic long and low-set hound-type ears, covered with hair.
Sussex Spaniels have a uniquely frowning expression in the breed, with a richly colored, single-tone liver or golden liver coat.
The Sussex Spaniels have almond shaped eyes that are either hazel or brown, that express a look of seriousness.
Sussex Spaniels have a moderate tail length, often held straight out or slightly elevated, but not curled over the back.
Irish Water Spaniel: This breed is known for its distinctive curly, liver-colored coat that is both water-resistant and hypoallergenic.
The Irish Water Spaniel has a topknot of long, loose curls that fall over its eyes and forehead.
This breed has a deep chest and strong, muscular body built for endurance and agility.
The Irish Water Spaniel has a long muzzle, almond-shaped eyes and a large, square, almost hairless nose.
The breed is characterized by its 'rat tail', which is thick at the base, covered with curls, but hairless from about a quarter towards the tip.
Irish Water Spaniels are larger and taller than most spaniels, males can stand up to 24 inches tall at the shoulder.
The breed has webbed feet which aids them in efficient swimming.
Kuvasz: Kuvasz dogs are large in size, typically weighing between 70 to 115 pounds.
This breed has a dense double coat, which is pure white and can be either straight or wavy.
They possess a dignified and robust stature, and are built for endurance and agility.
Kuvasz dogs have almond-shaped eyes that are dark and expressive, giving them a kind and intelligent look.
They have a black nose and their ears are V-shaped, medium in size, and slightly rounded at the tip.
This breed has a long tail set low, usually reaching down to the hocks.
The overall structure of a Kuvasz is well-balanced and harmonious, giving an impression of strength and agility.
Schipperke: Schipperkes are known for their small size, often weighing less than 20 pounds.
This brew is identified by their pure black, dense and harsh coat which is distinctive with a mane around the neck, culottes on the rear of each thigh, and a plume of hair on the tail.
They have a fox-like face with small, pointed ears that stand erect.
Schipperkes possess a unique silhouette due to their short build with the hind legs slightly longer than the front which gives a slope to the back.
They have dark brown, almond-shaped eyes that have a lively, intelligent expression.
Schipperkes typically have a confident and lively demeanor, they are known for their high energy and inquisitive nature.
Due to the dense nature of their coat, Schipperkes may appear larger or more robust in photos than their lightweight would suggest.
Groenendael dog: The breed is recognized by its long, straight and abundant black coat that gives an impression of sturdiness and elegance.
The distinct face has a flat skull, tapering muzzle, and medium-sized heart-shaped ears that are always erect and facing forward.
They are medium to large sized dogs, with a muscular and solid yet elegant body.
They have dark brown, almond-shaped eyes that reflect an alert and intelligent expression.
Their tail is strong and medium length; when in repose it hangs down, the end slightly curved. When excited, the dog raises it and waves it in a curve.
Characteristically, the Groenendael moves in a quick, agile trot, appearing to glide effortlessly across the ground.
Physically, these dogs are built for endurance and versatility, known to perform well in agility, obedience, herding, tracking, and even therapy work.
Malinois: Malinois are a medium to large breed of dogs, easily recognizable with their short and straight fawn to mahogany coat with black hairs spread throughout.
A unique characteristic in Malinois is their black mask and ears, significantly contrasting with their lighter body color.
Malinois have a strong and sturdy physique with noticeable muscularity, highlighting their strength and agility.
They possess a square body shape with the length and height at the withers giving a near to equal ratio.
Their eye color is usually in different shades of brown, ranging from dark to lighter tones, and their gaze often portrays alertness and intelligence.
The ears of Malinois are distinctively large and erect giving them a lively and active expression.
Their tails are typically long and strong with the tailbone reaching to the hock and are slightly curved upwards.
Briard: Briards are large-sized dogs, known for their long, wavy and shiny coats that usually come in various shades of fawn, black, and sometimes grey.
One distinctive characteristic of the Briard is their eyebrows which are bushy and their long facial fur, giving them a distinct, almost human-like face.
Briards have a strong and muscular body structure, fitting for their herding background.
Briard's eyes are usually darker, and they are known for their 'gaze', which they use for herding animals.
Briards have upright ears, that are usually covered by their long fur. The ears can be cropped or left natural.
They have a long tail, sometimes featuring a slight hook at the end which is usually covered with the long, wavy fur.
The Briard's four limbs are well-muscled and strong, which they use to move smoothly and at a quick pace.
Australian Kelpie: The breed has a double coat, which can be black, black and tan, red, red and tan, blue, blue and tan, fawn, fawn and tan, or cream.
Kelpies have a compact body and well-developed limbs. They are known for their agility and stamina, which is evident in their athletic appearance.
Kelpies have pricked ears, almond-shaped eyes, and an expressive face.
The breed's tail is medium length and curves upwards slightly.
The distinctive cat-like feet of a Kelpie is a unique attribute of the breed.
Despite their tough exterior, Kelpies are generally energetic, friendly, and intelligent.
Australian Kelpies are typically seen in action, as they are working dogs bred for mustering and droving with little guidance, and are often associated with the Australian outback.
Komondor: The Komondor is a large, white-colored dog breed known for its unique, corded coat that resembles dreadlocks or a mop.
The Komondor's coat is dense and long, providing protection from weather and predators.
The breed is robust and muscular, built for strength and endurance. Males can reach a height of up to 31.5 inches at the shoulder, while females are somewhat smaller.
Despite their size and strength, Komondorok (plural of Komondor) are known for their calm and steady temperament.
The Komondor has a large, broad head and a black nose. Its eyes are almond-shaped and brown, often hidden by the fur.
The breed has medium-sized ears that hang down close to its face, blending into its coat.
The Komondor's tail is long and hangs low, typically reaching hock length.
Old English Sheepdog: This breed is known for its long and thick coat, that often covers the eyes and is usually gray, blue or silver in color with white markings.
They are large in size, typically weighing between 60-100 pounds, which can be used as a reference scale when comparing to other objects in the picture.
This breed has a strong, compact body and they are slightly longer than they are tall.
Their tails are commonly docked to a very short length in places where docking is still legal.
They have a distinctive bear-like gait due to their herd dog heritage.
This breed has a large and square head with a capacious skull.
This breed has small, round feet with well-arched toes.
Shetland Sheepdog: Shetland Sheepdogs are instantly recognizable for their rough, thick double coat which usually comes in shades of sable, black, and blue merle.
Shetland Sheepdogs, similar to other herding dogs, have a muscular build that supports quickness and agility.
The Shetland Sheepdog has a characteristic 'mane' of hair around its neck, which is thicker and longer comparing to the hair on the rest of its body.
Shetland Sheepdogs have small, almond-shaped eyes that are typically dark, however, blue merle dogs may have blue or odd eyes.
The Shetland Sheepdog has a distinctive face with a tapered muzzle, a black nose and ears that bend slightly at the tip.
The Shetland Sheepdog is typically medium sized, standing between 13 to 16 inches at the shoulder.
The Shetland Sheepdog has a bushy tail that feathers out and upwards, but does not curl over the back.
collie: Collies are known for their distinct facial features, marked by a pointed snout and perky ears that stand erect or are tipped over.
Recognizable by the double coat of hair with a long and flowing outer coat and a soft undercoat. Coat colours can include sable and white, blue merle, white, and tri-color (black, white, and tan).
Rough Collies have a characteristic mane of hair around the neck and chest area, giving them a lion-like appearance.
The relative size of a collie is large; they are medium to large-sized dogs compared to other breeds.
They possess intelligent, expressive eyes that come in colors of blue or brown or a mix of both (one blue and one brown eye).
Collies are known for their lean and athletic body shape, with a deep chest and strong legs ideal for herding and agility.
They have a long bushy tail that is usually carried low unless the dog is alert or excited.
Border Collie: Border Collies are medium-sized dogs, typically weighing between 30 and 45 pounds.
They generally have a distinctive two-layer coat, which can be smooth or rough, and is often black and white in color.
They are known for their highly intelligent and active nature, requiring ample mental and physical stimulation.
Their ears can be straight or slightly bent, and their eyes can be a dark brown or, in some individuals, a striking blue.
They have a muscular, athletic build, signaling their readiness for activity or work.
The Border Collie's movement is graceful and tireless, with minimal lifting of their feet from the ground when at a fast trot.
They have a medium-length tail that ends in a curve, often raising when they are excited or alert.
Bouvier des Flandres dog: These dogs have a solid, sturdy build and powerful presence.
Characteristic for this breed are the dark, oval eyes and a heavy beard and moustache that cover their face.
Their body is covered with a thick double coat, which is weather-resistant. The coat color can range from fawn to black, passing through salt and pepper, gray and brindle.
Bouviers have broad skulls, a well-developed muzzle and their triangular-shaped ears are set high.
These dogs have strong muscular necks and wide, deep chests with robust, powerful legs, enabling them to be efficient working dogs.
Their tail is typically docked, but in countries where docking is forbidden, the tail should curve slightly upward.
Their gait is free, proud, and well-balanced due to their powerful legs and strong body.
Rottweiler: Rottweilers are large size dogs, known for their robust and powerful appearance.
They have a dense, straight and coarse black coat with clearly defined rust to mahogany markings on their cheeks, muzzles, chest, legs, and above their eyes.
Rottweilers have a broad head with a rounded forehead and a straight, strong, and wide muzzle.
Rottweilers have deep-set, almond-shaped eyes that are dark brown in color.
Their ears are medium-sized, pendant, triangular in shape, and wide apart, set high on the head.
They have a straight, thick, and robust tail that is usually leveled with their back.
Rottweilers have a muscular, broad, and deep chest, and their backs are straight and strong.
German Shepherd Dog: They are usually seen with tan and black or red and black coat. However, all-black and all-white German shepherd dogs also exist.
They are characteristically large-sized breed. Adult German Shepherds have a height ranging from 22 to 26 inches at the withers.
They are well-structured, strong, and muscular. Its body is elongated, with strong, straight legs.
German Shepherds have large, upright ears and almond-shaped, dark eyes. Their expression is often alert and intelligent.
German Shepherds have a thick and dense fur coat which can either be medium or long-haired.
They have a bushy tail that hangs down and curves slightly upwards at the end.
German Shepherds are renowned for their intelligence and versatility. They can be seen performing various roles, from police dogs to guide dogs for the blind.
Dobermann: Dobermanns are medium-to-large breed dogs known for their sleek and muscular body structure, standing between 24 to 28 inches at the shoulder.
This breed is traditionally recognized by its short, thin, and glossy coat which is usually black, red, blue, or fawn with rust-colored markings on the face, chest, paws, and tail.
They have a long muzzle and powerful jaw structure, and their teeth meet in a scissor bite.
Dobermanns have a distinctively cropped, upright ear setting, and traditionally have a docked tail, though this practice is now often avoided.
They are known for their alert and intelligent expression, with dark, medium-sized, almond-shaped eyes.
Prominent characteristics of the breed include a broad chest and a well-defined, slim waist.
The Dobermann gait is traditionally considered a trot, showcasing their balanced and efficient movement.
Miniature Pinscher: Miniature Pinschers are small dogs, with adult males and females generally weighing between 8 - 12 pounds.
They have a compact, muscular body with a smooth, short coat that comes in colors ranging from solid red, stag red (red with black), to black and rust or chocolate and rust.
Miniature Pinschers have high-set ears that are either cropped to stand erect or left natural, folding over as a small drop ear.
They have dark, bright and well-shaped eyes that convey an energetic personality.
Miniature Pinschers have a distinctive proud, robust gait that is sometimes referred to as a 'hackney gait', named after the horse breed with a similar prancing movement.
They have a thin tapering tail that is usually docked in countries where this practice is allowed.
Miniature Pinschers have a distinctive pointed face, with a tapered muzzle that gives the breed a fox-like expression.
Greater Swiss Mountain Dog: They are large and robust, with a strong and muscular body that is slightly longer than it is tall.
The breed is known for its distinct tri-color coat, which is predominantly black with white and rust markings.
The dog's head is powerful and solid, with a broad flat skull, and the muzzle is straight and strong.
The dogs have almond-shaped, medium-sized eyes that are dark brown.
The ears of Swissies are medium-sized, set high, triangular in shape, and gently rounded at the tip. When the dog is at attention, the ears are brought forward and raised at the base.
The tail of the breed is thick from root to end, tapering to a point, and carried in a downward curve or straight at rest and can be carried higher when the dog is excited or moving.
This breed of dog shows great joy in physical activity, often evidenced by a slight wag of the tail and a sparkling eye.
Bernese Mountain Dog: Bernese Mountain Dogs are known for their tri-color coat, typically black, white, and rust.
This breed is large, typically weighing between 70 and 115 pounds as adults.
These dogs have a thick double coat, which keeps them warm in cold weather.
Bernese Mountain Dogs have a distinctively gentle and affable expression, with dark, almond-shaped eyes.
They have medium-long straight fur with longer hair, or 'feathers', on their legs, belly and tail.
The breed is known for their strong and muscular build, designed for hard work such as pulling carts, which was their origin task in Swiss farms.
They have a broad head with a slight furrow and straight nose bridge, and their ears are medium-sized, triangular, set high, and rounded at the tips.
Appenzeller Sennenhund: This breed is medium-sized with a height of 17 to 23 inches and a weight of 49 to 70 pounds.
These dogs have a thick and glossy double coat that is black or brown with symmetrical white and rust markings.
The breed has a solid build with a broad chest, a muscular and straight back, and a deep-set chest.
They have a distinctive tricolor coat, with a black or brown base color, white chest and feet, and distinctive tan markings on the eyebrows, cheeks, and legs.
This breed has small, triangular ears that sit high on the head and are gently rounded at the tips.
They have dark brown eyes with an alert and lively expression.
Appenzeller Sennenhunds possess a bushy tail that often curls over the back when the dog is excited or in motion.
Entlebucher Sennenhund: This breed is recognized by its tri-colored coat, featuring primarily black with white and tan markings.
The breed typically has a compact, strong, and agile body, suitable for its original purpose of herding and guarding.
The size of the Entlebucher Sennenhund ranges from medium to large, with males standing 17-21 inches tall and females slightly shorter.
The breed has a distinctively dense, short and sleek coat that provides weather resistance.
Entlebucher Sennenhunds have broad heads with a slightly rounded skull, and their dark brown eyes are small and lively.
The breed has a unique feature that the tail is often naturally bobbed or may be docked in countries where it is permitted.
The breed is known for its energetic and active behavior, often seen participating in various activities and sports.
Boxer: Boxers are medium to large-sized breed of working dogs, with strong, muscular bodies.
The breed is characterized by a strong jaw with a perfect underbite, which was historically used for holding onto large game.
The coat is smooth and tight-fitting, colors are fawn, brindled, or white, with or without white markings.
The head is the most distinctive and the most valued in overall appearance with wrinkles when at attention or alert.
They have a broad and deep chest extending to the elbows for a roomy heart. The back is short and straight.
Their ears, when not cropped, are wide, top-set and not too close to the head. They are loyal dogs and enjoy being in the company of their owners.
The Boxer's tail is set high and usually docked. A Boxer's walk is firm, elastic, noble and powerful.
Bullmastiff: Bullmastiffs have a powerful build, lending to their past as guard dogs, and are known to have great strength despite their generally calm demeanour.
These dogs have a short, dense coat of fur that comes in colors such as fawn, red, or brindle.
Bullmastiffs are large, with males standing 25-27 inches tall at the shoulder and females standing 24-26 inches tall.
They have a broad and wrinkled forehead with a short, wide, dark muzzle.
Bullmastiffs have a very distinct black face mask that does not extend over the eyes and ears, with a dark muzzle.
Their body is compact with a high set tail that is neither too long nor too short, but is thick at the base tapering to a point.
They have deep set, dark hazel eyes with an intelligent and alert expression.
Tibetan Mastiff: Tibetan Mastiffs are known for their thick and heavy double coat which comes in a range of colors including black, brown, red, and grey.
Tibetan Mastiffs are large dogs with males standing as high as 33 inches at the shoulder.
Tibetan Mastiffs have broad heads with deep-set, almond-shaped eyes that are usually brown.
They have a noticeably sort of mane of hair around their neck and shoulders, particularly in males, making them look even more lionlike.
Tibetan Mastiffs possess a solemn but kind expression, with a slight wrinkling of skin on the forehead when alerted.
They have V-shaped ears that droop down and a tail that curls over the back.
Despite their imposing size, Tibetan mastiffs are known for their calm and gentle temperament.
French Bulldog: They are typically small to medium sized dogs, with a sturdy compact build and a substantial bone structure.
French bulldogs have a striking bat-ear, which is broad at the base and rounded at the top.
Their eyes are dark and round, and sit slightly above the line of the squarish muzzle.
They have a characteristic flat face and a short, wrinkled muzzle.
They typically have a shiny and smooth short coat, and can come in a variety of colors such as brindle, fawn, or white.
Their tail is naturally short, straight or screw-shaped and tapering from a wide base to a nearly pointed tip.
They often exhibit behaviors that are indicative of their playful and affectionate nature.
Great Dane: Great Danes are one of the world's tallest breeds, easily recognizable by their large size; males can stand up to 32 inches high at the shoulder, and females are only slightly smaller.
They have a strong, square jaw and a rectangular head, known for its expressive eyes and alert ears which can either be cropped or left natural.
Great Danes have a smoothly muscled body which showcases their power and athleticism, with a long tail that is thin and tapered to a point.
They have a short and sleek coat that can come in a variety of colors including brindle, fawn, blue, black, harlequin (an irregular pattern of black patches over a white background), and mantle.
The breed is known for its friendly and patient nature, making it a great family companion despite its large size.
Great Danes are often seen in a proud and elegant stance, which, combined with their size, gives them an imposing presence.
It has very recognizable, long and slender legs, which provide both strength and speed, contributing to its graceful trot.
St. Bernard: Bernard. They are known for their large size, often weighing between 140 and 260 pounds.
Bernard. The breed typically has a broad and powerful body structure.
Bernard. St. Bernard dogs have a dense and muscular build, with a unique square head shape.
Bernard. Their eyes are usually dark brown and express a kind and gentle demeanor.
Bernard. Their fur is usually a mixture of white and darker patches, often brown or reddish-brown.
Bernard. They have a distinctive large head with a wrinkled forehead and a short muzzle.
Bernard. The St. Bernard's ears are medium-sized and set at the top of their head, hanging close to the cheeks.
husky: Huskies are known for their striking blue or multicolored eyes and unique markings.
They are medium-sized dogs, generally weighing between 35 to 60 pounds, with a healthy, athletic build.
The Husky breed has a thick coat which comes in a multitude of colors and marking patterns, including black, grey, sable, and white.
Huskies carry a wolf-like appearance with a strong, muscular body structure and sharp, erect ears.
They are known for their high energy levels and are often seen exploring or participating in physical activities.
Huskies have a bushy tail that often curls over their back.
The relative size of a husky is larger compared to other objects in the image.
Alaskan Malamute: Alaskan Malamutes have a powerful, sturdy body built for stamina and strength.
They stand well over the pads, and have a strong, deep chest and a muscular neck and shoulders.
They are known for their broad head with a large muzzle and erect ears.
Their eyes are almond shaped and are varied shades of brown; however, the darker eye is preferred.
The coat is thick with a coarse guard coat of sufficient length to protect a woolly undercoat.
Alaskan Malamutes are of various colors. The most common colors are various shades of gray and white, sable and white, black and white, red and white, or solid white.
They have a plumed tail that is carried over the back.
Siberian Husky: They are known for their striking blue or multi-colored eyes and their distinctive facial masks.
Huskies have a thick double fur coat that can be black, grey, or red on the top coat and is white on the undercoat.
The relative size of a Siberian Husky is medium to large compared to other objects in the image.
They have erect, 'wolf-like' ears and a straight, bushy tail.
Huskies are often depicted in a running or playing posture due to their high energy and agility.
Their body structure shows strength and stamina with an athletic and compact body built for work and endurance.
They have a friendly and gentle demeanor that is noticeable in their expressions.
Dalmatian: Dalmatians are easily identifiable by their striking coat pattern, which consists of black or liver spots on a white background.
Dalmatians are of a distinctive breed with a strong, muscular body and a square build.
They possess a unique set of wide-set round eyes that can be either brown or blue.
The relative size of a Dalmatian is larger when compared to many other breeds, adding to its commanding presence.
The breed's distinctive ears are set high on the head, are of a moderate size, and are floppy, hanging downwards.
Dalmatians have a sturdy and well-built body, with a square-proportioned build, contributing to their endurance and speed.
They exhibit a rather active and playful behavior, often seen in an energetic state.
Affenpinscher: Affenpinschers are small-sized dogs usually not exceeding 13 pounds in weight.
Affenpinschers have a distinctive monkey-like facial expression, hence their name which translates to 'monkey terrier' in German.
Their coats are typically black, but can come in other colors like gray, silver, red, black and tan, or beige.
Affenpinschers have a dense and shaggy coat giving them a somewhat scruffy look.
They have prominent bushy eyebrows and a shaggy beard, contributing to their unique appearance.
Their ears are either cropped to a point or naturally occur as drop ears.
They have a short muzzle and black nose.
Basenji: Basenjis are small to medium-sized dogs, typically weighing 20-25 pounds and standing 16-17 inches tall at the shoulder.
Basenjis have a short, sleek coat that comes in several colors, including red, black, brindle, and tri-color (black, white, and tan).
One of the most distinctive features of a Basenji is their wrinkled forehead and expressive eyes, which are often described as 'thoughtful' or 'worried'.
Basenjis have a unique tail that curls tightly over their back, often forming a double curl.
They have erect, pointed ears that contribute to their alert and intelligent expression.
Basenjis have a lean and muscular body, which gives them a graceful and athletic appearance.
Compared to other objects in the picture, the Basenji is relatively small in size.
pug: Pugs are small, muscular dogs with a compact, square body and a short, thick and often curled tail.
Pugs have a broad, round and wrinkled face with large, bulging eyes. The wrinkles are most pronounced around the forehead and nose.
They are known for their distinctive pushed-in nose, which gives them a unique snorting and snuffling sound while breathing.
Pugs typically have a soft, double coat that can be fawn, silver, apricot, or black in color. The darker 'masks' and ears are among their distinguishable features.
They are often recognized by their short, stocky stature - they are generally 10 to 14 inches tall at the shoulder.
Pugs usually have a friendly and outgoing personality, showing a playful and affectionate demeanour in images.
The physical traits of a pug like the large round head, small ears folded with the front edges facing towards the nose and the slightly undershot jaw are key identifiers.
Leonberger: Leonbergers are large-sized dogs with a height of 26 to 31 inches and a weight of around 90-170 pounds.
This breed is known for their lion-like mane around the neck and chest, especially in males. Their fur color ranges from lion-yellow to red to sand.
Leonbergers have a friendly and gentle expression on their face, with medium-sized, deep-set brown eyes.
They possess a strong, muscular, and well-balanced body, with a deep chest, well-sprung ribs, and a well-muscled back.
Their ears are medium-sized and hang close to the head.
Leonbergers have a thick double coat, which is water-resistant, and a bushy tail that usually rests below the level of the back and reaches at least to the hocks.
They have straight front legs and strong, muscular hind legs with well-angulated stifle (knee) and hock joints.
Newfoundland dog: Newfoundland dogs are large, with most standing at 26 to 28 inches at the shoulder and weighing between 130 to 150 pounds.
They are known for their thick, water-resistant double coat, which is usually found in black, brown, gray, or a black and white color known as Landseer.
Their broad, massive heads feature a pronounced stop and strong muzzle, with small, deep-set, generally dark brown eyes.
Newfoundland dogs are characterized by their large and heavily boned body with a muscular build, deep chest and strong, straight legs.
They have large, webbed paws which make them excellent swimmers.
Their tail is strong and broad at the base, covered with dense hair, and hangs down slightly curved at rest.
Newfoundland dogs carry a kind, gentle and sweet-natured expression that reflects their calm and docile personality.
Great Pyrenees dog: They are known for their thick white coats that are weather resistant, needing regular grooming and brushing.
These dogs have a large and powerful build, usually weighing between 85 to 100 pounds.
Great Pyrenees dogs have a distinct bear-like facial appearance with a flat skull, slightly curved muzzle, and medium-sized, almond-shaped eyes that are typically dark brown.
They are known for their calm and patient demeanor, often appearing majestically serene in photos.
These dogs usually have fully-erect, medium-sized ears that are set at eye level and are somewhat rounded at the tips.
These dogs have a full tail that is typically plume-like and is carried low while relaxed, but is arched over the back when they are active.
Great Pyrenees dogs are well-balanced and move smoothly despite their size, usually seen with a certain elegance due to their power and majesty.
Samoyed: Samoyeds are known for their thick, white fluffy coats that give them their characteristic 'smiling' appearance.
The Samoyed has a wedge-shaped head with a strong and muscular neck.
Samoyeds have deep-set, dark colored almond-shaped eyes which portray a friendly and intelligent expression.
Samoyeds have upright, triangular ears that are covered with hair.
The Samoyed has a strong, muscular body with a deep chest.
The tail is an important characteristic of the Samoyed, which is carried curled over their back most of the times.
Samoyeds are larger in size, typically measuring between 19 to 24 inches in height.
Pomeranian: Pomeranians are small dogs known for their fluffy double coat, typically a shade of orange or red but can also be in other colors like white, black, blue, or tan.
Pomeranians are easily identifiable by their wedge-shaped head with a short, pointed muzzle. Their almond-shaped eyes appear bright and alert.
They have small, erect ears on top of their head, giving them a characteristic fox-like appearance.
These dogs have a compact but sturdy body that looks larger than it is, thanks to their dense, puffy coat.
The Pomeranian's tail is its distinctive feature, it arches forward and rests on their back.
Pomeranians move with a smooth gait and are slightly bouncy while walking or running.
Despite their small size, Pomeranians are energetic and often seen playing or being active.
Chow Chow: They are medium to large-sized dogs known for their dense coat which can vary in colors such as red, black, blue, cinnamon, and cream.
Recognizing a Chow Chow can often be due to their unique blue-black tongue which is a distinguishing characteristic of the breed.
The Chow Chow has a dense and fluffy double coat, giving them a lion's mane appearance and robust stature.
They have a broad skull and small, rounded ears set wide apart.
The eyes of Chow Chows are typically dark and almond-shaped, set deep in the face.
A notable characteristic is their tail, which is high-set and curls over their back.
Their movement is often described as stilted or cat-like, due to their straight rear legs.
Keeshond: Keeshonden typically have a dense double coat that is gray, black, and cream in color, creating a 'spectacles' around their eyes.
The Keeshond is a medium-sized dog with a plumed tail that curls tightly over the back.
Keeshonden have a thick ruff around the neck, further enhancing the 'lion-like' appearance.
They are recognized for their expressive eyes which are almond-shaped and dark brown in color.
Keeshonden have a distinctive, wedge-shaped head with medium sized ears that stand erect.
The Keeshond's body is compact and short, with a deep chest and well-sprung ribs.
The Keeshond has medium bone structure and exhibits a well-balanced and sturdy stance.
brussels griffon: This breed is notable for its distinctive pug-like face, with large, round eyes, a flat nose, and a prominent underbite.
The breed has a dense coat that can be smooth or rough. The rough coat, also known as the Griffon Bruxellois, is longer and wiry, while the smooth coat, or the Petit BrabanÃ§on, is short and glossy.
The common colors for this breed are red, belge (mix of black and reddish brown), black and tan, and solid black.
They are small dogs, often weighing between 8 to 10 pounds and measuring up to 10 inches in height.
Despite their small size, these dogs have a sturdy and muscular build, with a balanced and square-shaped body.
This breed has small, thinly feathered ears that are usually semi-erect if they have not been cropped.
Their tail is typically docked to a medium length and is carried high, adding to their confident and lively demeanor.
Pembroke Welsh Corgi: Pembroke Welsh Corgis have a distinctive appearance due to their short legs and long body. Their stature is typically low to the ground.
They are known for their rich-colored coat which can vary in shades of red, sable, fawn, and black and tan. Some may have white markings on parts of the body.
This breed typically has a straight, dense undercoat and a coarse outer coat, which can be of varying lengths across its body.
They have a relatively large, expressive head with wide-set, round, medium sized brown eyes, which gives them an alert and intelligent expression.
They have a signature tail which is usually docked very short, often making it look like they have no tail.
The ears of a Pembroke Welsh Corgi are a distinctive feature, fairly large in proportion to its head and set widely apart. They are erect at the base with slightly rounded tips.
Pembroke Welsh Corgis are known for their friendly and playful nature, and are often shown in motion, either running or walking enthusiastically.
Cardigan Welsh Corgi: These dogs are recognizable for their long bodies and relatively short and sturdy legs, often likened to a loaf of bread on legs.
Cardigans are typically larger than their cousins, the Pembroke Welsh Corgis, and have a heavier bone structure.
These dogs have a wide array of coat colors, but commonly seen ones are red, sable, brindle, black, and blue merle.
They have a thick, medium-length double coat that requires regular grooming to keep it healthy and looking its best.
Cardigans have large, prominent ears that stand erect on top of their head, contributing to their alert and expressive look.
They have a long tail which is another distinctive feature as most Pembroke Welsh Corgis are born with a short tail or have it docked.
The Cardigan's eyes are another unique feature, often darker in color with an oval shape and displaying an intelligent and inquisitive expression.
Toy Poodle: Toy Poodles are one of the smallest types of poodles with a height of no more than 10 inches.
They are known for their curly and dense coat which comes in various colours such as black, white, brown, and grey.
The coat is often styled in a distinctive clip such as the puppy clip, continental clip or English saddle clip.
They have long ears that hang down and are often covered with curly fur.
Toy Poodles have a compact body with a level back and a tail that is often docked.
They have dark, oval shaped eyes and a square, well-proportioned body.
Despite their size, Toy Poodles are known for their intelligent and active nature, typically seen as alert and attuned to their surroundings.
Miniature Poodle: They are one of the three sizes of Poodles, and are between 10 and 15 inches tall at the shoulder.
They are known for their thick, curly or wavy coat that comes in many color variations, such as white, black, apricot, cream, blue, and sable.
Poodles have a distinctive haircut due to their history as water retrievers. The 'pom-poms' on their body were meant to keep their joints warm in cold water.
They have an athletic build and a prancing gait.
They have long, flat ears that hang close to their head.
Poodles have dark oval-shaped eyes that give them an alert and intelligent expression.
They have a straight muzzle with a moderate stop and a relatively large and round nose that is the same color as their coat.
Standard Poodle: These dogs are known for their curly, dense, and harsh textured coat which can come in a variety of solid colors such as white, black, apricot and grey.
The Standard Poodle is the largest of the three Poodle varieties, with males standing over 15 inches and females slightly smaller.
These dogs have a distinctive topknot on their heads, usually tied up with a band or styled into a pompom.
Their ears are long, wide, thickly feathered and hang close to the head.
They have a trim, athletic build and are noticeably elegantly and proudly carried.
Standard Poodles have almond-shaped eyes that are dark in color and have an alert and intelligent expression.
They are known for their stylish clips showcasing a lion-like look in hindquarters with areas of the coat left long, and the rest is clipped short.
Mexican hairless dog (xoloitzcuintli): As the name suggests, one of the most noticeable characteristics of this breed is its lack of fur, known for their smooth, hairless skin, although there is also a coated variety.
They are known for their bat-like ears that stand erect, giving them a distinctive silhouette.
Xoloitzcuintli have a strong, sturdy, and lean body physique, ranging from toy to miniature to standard sizes.
They have a pretty strong, straight back with a level topline and a long tail that is set low.
Their eyes are almond-shaped and can come in varying shades of brown.
Xoloitzcuintli are known for their gait, which is smooth, effortless, and with good reach in front and drive behind.
Being hairless, the skin of the breed is prone to dryness so it often appears moisturized or oiled.
grey wolf: The grey wolf has a dense and straight fur coat that can vary in color, but is commonly grey with tints of brown, however can also be seen in pure white, red and black.
This animal is noticeably large, with males typically ranging from 66-180 pounds and females being slightly smaller.
Grey wolves have a distinctive body shape with a broad skull, pointed ears, elongated snout, a large trunk, and a bushy tail.
Grey wolves have a set of strong and sharp teeth which are highly efficient for hunting and tearing through raw meat.
They travel in packs, thus images with multiple wolves may indicate a grey wolf.
Their eyes are typically yellow-gold in color, offering a striking contrast against their darker fur.
Grey wolves are generally quite active with most activity occurring at dawn and dusk. In images, they might be seen in various stages of hunting, running, or playing.
Alaskan tundra wolf: These wolves are known for their thick, dense white fur that allows them to blend in with the snowy environment of the Alaskan tundra. Though their fur can also appear in other colors such as grey and black.
These wolves are large, with males reaching lengths of 7 feet from nose to tail tip and weight up to 200 pounds.
The Alaskan tundra wolf has a broad, heavy muzzle, and large, cupped, rounded ears that alert them to nearby sounds.
They are known for their big, round and yellow eyes, which are adapted for nighttime hunting.
This wolf has long, heavy limbs and a deep chest which equip it well for navigating the challenging winter terrain and chasing prey.
These carnivorous animals are usually found in packs, oftentimes seen with other Alaskan tundra wolves in the image.
They are known for their strong predatory behavior and typically seen in certain habitats such as tundra, forests and some coastal areas of Alaska.
red wolf or maned wolf: Red wolves are medium-sized canids with a slender, elegant build.
They have a distinguishing red or tawny color on their upper coat.
Red wolves have pointed, upright ears and long legs relative to their body size.
The tail of a red wolf usually has a black or dark tip.
Red wolves have a broad nose pad with a shallow angle between the upper jaw and nasal bone.
They are of medium height, shorter than gray wolves but larger than coyotes.
Eye color varies but is typically yellow or amber.
maned wolf: Maned wolves are the tallest of the wild canids, with long, slender legs and a distinctive mane running from the back of the head to the shoulders.
Their pelage is reddish brown to golden orange on the sides, with long, black legs and a distinctive black mane.
They have a marked white 'bib' beneath the throat and a bushy, white-tipped tail.
Maned wolves have large, rounded ears and a long, pointed muzzle.
Their eyes are typically golden in color.
The maned wolf is notable for its distinctive odor, which has led to it being colloquially referred to as a 'skunk wolf'.
Maned wolves typically live in grasslands, scrub prairies, and forests.
coyote: Coyotes typically have a greyish-brown to yellowish-gray color on the upper body and light grey to cream-colored underside.
They have a slender, elongated body supported by powerful, slim legs.
Their tail is bushy and black-tipped and is generally carried low, below the level of the back.
Coyotes have large, pointed ears set wide apart on the top of the head, which tend to be more propped-up than the ears of their close relatives, dogs, and wolves.
The coyote's eyes are yellow with round pupils and can have an intense, penetrating gaze.
The coyote's paws are relatively small in comparison to its body size, and the tracks it leaves behind are usually in a relatively straight line.
Coyotes are known for their distinctive vocalizations, which include howls, yips, yowls, and sometimes 'barks', although this might not be apparent from a single image.
dingo: Dingoes are medium-sized canines, typically weighing between 15 to 20 kilograms.
Dingoes usually have a ginger or tan fur, but they can also be found in shades of black, white, and creamy yellow.
Dingo's ears are naturally erect and pointed, an attribute often used for alertness and communication.
They have a bushy tail that is slightly curved towards the back.
Dingoes are known for their distinctive elongated snout, which differentiates them from other domesticated dogs.
The eyes of a Dingo are usually almond-shaped and can be colored from yellow to orange.
Dingoes are usually seen alone or in small packs in their natural habitat, which is a broad range of environments all across Australia.
dhole: Dholes are canids, a type of mammal known for their keen sense of smell and strong, lean bodies.
Dholes' coats are reddish-brown in color, but can also range from a golden yellow to a dark grey.
A dhole's size is comparable to that of a German shepherd, and they have physical builds suited for stamina and speed.
Dholes have bushy tails that are more than half the length of their bodies.
Dholes have pointed ears and a long snout, typical characteristics of carnivorous species.
They have white underparts and a black, round spot right at the base of the tail.
Dholes are mostly found in the forests and grasslands of Asia.
African wild dog: They are known for their distinct coat patterns, which are a mix of red, black, white, brown and tan markings. No two individuals have the exact same pattern.
They have a body shape similar to a domestic dog, with long legs and a lean build.
They often live in packs, so pictures of African wild dogs may show multiple individuals together.
They have large, rounded ears covered in fur that differ significantly from the pointed or floppy ears of many other dogs.
They have a bushy tail with a white tip, which is characteristic of the species.
Relative to other objects in the photo, African wild dogs are medium to large-sized animals.
They are typically found in natural environments like grasslands, savannas, and lightly wooded areas.
hyena: Hyenas are known for their distinctively sloping build, with a front part that is higher than the back end.
Hyenas possess a robust and powerful body structure, capable of running at high speeds and withstanding injuries.
Hyenas have short, coarse fur that comes in a variety of patterns, ranging from solid to spotted or striped.
Hyenas have large, powerful jaws filled with sharp teeth, used for crushing bones and tearing meat.
The relative size of hyenas is larger compared to other mammals depicted in the image.
Hyenas have large, rounded ears that are often marked with nicks or scars.
Hyenas have a bushy tail that they can hold up as a sign of aggression or excitement.
red fox: Red foxes are known for their bright red or orange coat, but they can also have patches of white and black fur, especially on their chest and tail tip.
Red foxes have a distinctively pointed and elongated snout that's relative to the size of their head.
The relative size of red foxes is smaller compared to other larger wildlife, yet larger compared to small pets and rodents.
Red foxes have large, pointy ears that are usually erect and forward-facing, a feature that helps them listen for prey in their environment.
Red foxes have long, bushy tails, often with a white tip. These tails are multifunctional, helping foxes balance and keep warm during the winter.
Red foxes have slender, leggy bodies that enable them to run fast and jump high, aiding in hunting and escape from predators.
Red foxes have dark, almond-shaped eyes that contribute to their sharp and alert facial expressions.
kit fox: Kit foxes are characterized by their small size compared to other types of foxes, typically weighing between 3.5 to 5.5 pounds.
Kit foxes have a slender, streamlined physique with a brown coat that blends into desert environments.
They are known for their large ears, which are used for heat dissipation in their arid habitats.
Kit foxes have black-tipped tails, distinguishing them from other fox species.
The kit fox has a long and bushy tail, which is typically longer than half its body length.
Kit foxes have slight, elongated bodies with long, thin legs, which allow them to run swiftly over the desert sands.
The kit fox has distinctive broad, rounded ears, which not only help in dissipating heat but also in hearing the movements of their prey.
Arctic fox: The Arctic fox is characterized by its small size, with a head and body length of 46 to 68 cm, a tail length of up to 30 cm, and a weight of 3.2 to 9.4 kg.
One distinctive feature of the Arctic fox is its pure white fur in winters, which provides excellent camouflage in snowy environments.
In the summer, the Arctic fox changes its coat to match the tundra's brown or grey landscape, a colour morph which is often called 'Blue fox'.
Its body shape is compact with short legs and a bushy tail that it uses to wrap around itself for warmth.
The Arctic fox also has a very dense fur which is the warmest of all mammals.
Its small, furry ears are another adaptation to prevent heat loss in the harsh Arctic environment.
The size of Arctic fox is smaller in comparison to other objects or animals in the image.
grey fox: Grey foxes are known for their grizzled grey fur on their bodies, but they also have reddish-brown fur on their legs, chest and neck.
Grey foxes have sharp, pointed faces with large ears.
They have a long, bushy tail, often with a black stripe down the top and a dark tip.
Grey foxes are medium-sized for foxes, typically weighting between 7 to 13 pounds.
They are known for their ability to climb trees, which is unusual for foxes.
Grey foxes typically have black, oval pupils in their eyes.
The grey fox is predominantly nocturnal or crepuscular and makes its den in hollow trees, stumps or appropriated burrows during the day.
tabby cat: Tabby cats can be identified by their distinctive coat patterns, which typically consist of stripes, swirls, and dots in varying patterns.
The tabby cat can come in a range of colors, from brown, grey, cream to orange or red, often mixed with whites.
Tabby cats usually have an 'M' shaped marking on their forehead.
A tabby's eyes are usually clear and bright; their color can vary, however, green or golden are quite common.
Tabbies have a wide range of body types, from slender and athletic to the more sturdy and thickset.
The size of a tabby cat can greatly vary, but they can often be identified as medium to large-sized cats.
Tabbies have medium to long tails which usually end in a dark tip.
tiger cat: Tiger cats typically have a coat that is striped like a tiger, hence their name. This striped pattern, known as mackerel tabby, is the most common of all tabby patterns.
The body of the tiger cat is muscular and medium to large in size, with robust bone structure.
The eyes of a tiger cat are usually copper or gold, but can also occasionally be green.
Tiger cats usually have medium to long fur, though there are also short-haired varieties. Their fur is glossy and thick, providing good insulation.
The tail of the tiger cat is usually thick and bushy, with rings of color similar to those on the body.
Tiger cats can be a variety of colors including brown, silver, and red, all with a distinctive pattern of darker stripes.
Tiger cats have a strong jawline and high cheekbones, with the ears ideally forming an equilateral triangle with the upper face.
Persian cat: Persian cats come in a wide range of colors and patterns, but all have a sweet, rounded face with a snub nose and large round eyes, which are usually copper or blue.
Persian cats are known for their long, silky, and shiny coat which requires regular grooming to prevent matting.
They have a robust and muscular body type with a broad chest, short legs, and a short, thick tail with a rounded tip.
Persian cats have small ears compared to their head size, which are set low, wide apart, and have a broad base.
The relative size of a Persian cat is small compared to other objects in the image.
Persian cats are known for their calm and gentle behavior. They prefer serene environments and are not usually seen jumping or climbing.
Some Persian Cats have a flat or 'peke' face, characterized by a very flat nose, and forehead, and a somewhat protruding lower jaw, which may give them a frowning appearance.
Siamese cat: Siamese cats are known for their bright blue almond-shaped eyes.
Siamese cats have a short and glossy coat that is very fine in texture.
This breed is characterized by its distinctive color points on ears, face, paws, and tail, which are usually darker than the rest of their body.
Siamese cats have a slim, long, and muscular body.
Siamese cats have a wide range of body colors, but the most common is seal point, which is a fawn body with dark brown points.
The head of the Siamese is wedge-shaped, with a straight profile.
The relative size of Siamese cats is medium compared to other objects in the image.
Egyptian Mau: The Egyptian Mau is a medium-sized breed with a muscular, yet elegant body shape, and is known for being one of the few naturally spotted breeds of domestic cat.
Their coat colors can be silver, bronze or smoke, but the spots must be clearly contrasted with the base color.
The spots on an Egyptian Mau are random and vary in size and shape, appearing on the body, but not on the head, neck, and lower limbs.
They have distinctive facial markings, including mascara lines that extend from the corners of their eyes.
Their eyes are usually a green color, ranging from gooseberry green to a vivid emerald green.
One feature unique to the breed is a flap of skin extending from the flank to the back knee, providing for greater agility and length of stride.
They have a moderate wedge-shaped head with slightly rounded contours, medium to large ears, and almond-shaped eyes.
cougar: Cougars are large and lean animals, with males typically larger than females.
Cougars are mainly recognized by their tawny color, though they can range from brownish-grey to reddish with lighter parts on the underside.
Cougars have a small head with high-set ears and a black-tipped tail.
The cougar's body is designed for strength, with powerful hindquarters and a muscular physique.
Cougars have a distinct 'M' shaped marking above their eyes, which distinguishes them from other large cats.
Cougars have a long body with a tail that can be one third of its length.
The relative size of cougars is larger compared to other objects in the image.
lynx: Lynx are medium-sized wildcats known for their pointed ears, which are adorned with a distinctive black tuft at the top.
The fur coat of a lynx is typically yellow, brown or grey, and is often marked with spots especially in the lighter colored underside.
Lynx have a short tail with a black tip, which differentiates them from other wildcats.
The size of a lynx varies depending upon the individual species. Eurasian Lynx are larger and can reach over 60 pounds while Canadian and Iberian Lynx are generally smaller.
Lynx have large, padded paws which are adapted for moving through snowy terrains.
Their facial features are characterized by a ruff of fur beneath the neck, a beard-like feature which can give the face a triangular appearance.
They have bright green or yellowish eyes with vertical slits, which are well adapted for their nocturnal hunting lifestyle.
leopard: Leopards have a distinctive coat pattern of rosettes - clusters of dark, circular spots with a lighter centre, spread on a yellow to light-brown coat.
Leopards are known for their powerful build and muscular bodies that enable them to climb trees and swim well.
In comparison to other objects in the image, a leopard is of a considerable size.
Leopards have a long body and short legs, which lead to an elongated appearance compared to other big cats.
They have a large skull with strong jaw muscles, allowing them to carry heavy prey up trees.
They have bold, dark spots on their face, along with white underparts.
Unlike the similar-looking cheetah, leopards have a smaller, rounded head and smaller, fuller spots.
snow leopard: Snow leopards are large cats, known for their smoky-gray fur with black rosettes and spots.
They have relatively shorter legs and a longer tail, which is bushy and almost the same length as the body.
Snow leopards are notable for their round, wide-set eyes with vertical pupils, a feature unique among the big cats.
Snow leopards have a robust build, with males weighing around 60-120 pounds and females being slightly smaller.
Their coat is very dense and can change from a thick winter coat to a shorter summer coat.
Snow leopards are well adapted to their habitat in high altitudes, with features like enlarged nasal cavities for high-altitude respiration.
Their paws are broad and fur-covered for extra warmth and traction in their snowy, mountainous environment.
jaguar: Jaguars are large felines that are typically tan or orange with black spots, known as rosettes, because they are shaped like roses.
Jaguars are the third-largest wild cat species after the tiger and the lion. They are significant in size compared to many other objects in the picture.
The jaguar has a sturdy body, powerful jaws, and a large head; its legs are also relatively short and muscular compared to other big cats.
Jaguar's paws are broad with sharp, retractable claws.
Its eyes are a pale yellow or green often highlighted by a black 'eyeliner' marking.
The jaguar's tail is also generally shorter compared to other big cats; the tail aids in balancing and turning quickly while chasing prey.
Jaguars have a strong swimming ability and are often in proximity to water; they are also known for their ability to climb trees.
lion: Lions are large carnivores known for their tawny or light brown coats.
Male lions uniquely have a large mane of hair around their heads, the size and darkness can vary.
Lions have a large, muscular build and move with a distinctive gait.
Lions have a broad head with a high forehead region and a pronounced muzzle with whiskers.
The relative size of lions is typically larger compared to other objects or animals in the image.
Lions have very prominent and sharp canines used for hunting.
Lions have a long tail with a tuft of hair at the end.
tiger: Tigers are recognized by their distinct coat patterns, which have a base of orange or white with black or dark grey stripes.
Adult tigers are large and muscular, typically ranging from 5 to 10 feet in length, not including their long, thick tail, which adds another 3 to 4 feet.
Tigers have a methodical walk. When running or leaping, they exhibit exceptional agility, speed, and grace.
The tiger's face is distinctive, with a heavy muzzle, powerful jaws, and large, forward-facing eyes. They also have prominent whiskers and small round ears.
Tigers have broad, strong paws with five retractable claws on their forepaws and four on their hind paws.
Tiger's eyes are yellow to amber, surrounded by light fur that also lines the lower part of their face, while the rest of the face features fur of varying shades.
Tigers have a white spot on the back of their ears, which is thought to act as a false eye to deter potential predators from attacking.
cheetah: Cheetahs are characterized by a slender body and a small, rounded head making their overall physique designed for speed.
They have a distinctive 'tear mark' running from the inner corner of their eyes down to the sides of their mouth.
Cheetahs have a light body structure with a predominantly golden-yellow coat covered by black, evenly spaced spots.
They have a distinctive white-tipped tail with black spots, which often forms a unique pattern at the broader base end.
The relative size of a cheetah is bigger compared to other objects in the same image, but smaller than other bigger cats like lions and tigers.
Cheetahs are known for their unique running style, appearing to be almost airborne when sprinting at full speed.
They have a long and muscular tail that helps them maintain balance during a high-speed chase.
brown bear: Brown bears are characterized by their large body size, with adults typically weighing between 300 and 850 pounds.
Brown bears have a distinctive hump on their shoulders, which is a muscle mass used for digging and fighting.
They have long, curved claws that are stronger and longer than those of black bears. These are used for digging and catching prey.
The fur color of a brown bear can vary from a light cream color to almost black, though they are most commonly a medium to dark brown.
Brown bears have a wide, dish-shaped face with round ears.
Their eyes are relatively small, and their vision is thought to be similar to humans.
Brown bears are equipped with a powerful jaw, with large canines and grinding molars for a broad diet.
American black bear: These bears are generally dark brown or black, but can sometimes appear in shades ranging from white to cinnamon.
They have a large body with a characteristic bulky build and short, stocky legs.
The relative size of the American black bear is much larger compared to other objects in the image.
They have a short tail, that is often hidden beneath their thick fur.
These bears have large, rounded ears which stand upright on their head.
They have a prominent snout with a straight facial profile and small eyes.
American black bears have sharp claws useful for climbing trees, a behavior often observed in this species.
polar bear: Polar bears are distinctive for their pure white, thick fur covering their entire body, allowing them to blend into snowy environments.
The relative size of polar bears is larger compared to most other objects or species in the image.
Polar bears stand out due to their large size, as they are the largest species of bear.
Polar bears have a heavy body, a large head with a pointed snout, and small ears.
One distinct characteristic of polar bears is their black nose which is often visible against their white fur.
Polar bears have large and powerful forelimbs which they use for swimming and hunting.
They have thick pads and claws on their paws for navigating icy terrain.
sloth bear: Sloth bears have a distinctive shaggy black coat, with a mane around the face, and long, sickle-shaped claws.
They are known for their white or cream-colored chest marks, which can vary in shape and size from one individual to another.
Their relative size is larger compared to other objects in the image.
Sloth bears have a protruding and long snout, which is a key characteristic to differentiate it from other bear species.
This type of bear has lower lips that can be stretched out, for eating insects, and are missing upper incisors to create a perfect vacuum.
It has large, rounded ears that are noticeably larger than those of other bear species.
Sloth bears are noticeably hirsute and their fur can appear untidy.
mongoose: Mongooses generally have a slender, elongated body, short legs, and a long tapered tail.
Mongooses are usually brown or grey in color, with some species having markings such as stripes or spots.
Most species of mongoose have a furry coat that is short and coarse, but some varieties, like the Indian gray mongoose, have a much longer and denser coat.
The head of a mongoose is typically wedge-shaped with a pointed snout, small ears, and relatively large, forward-set eyes for excellent forward vision.
The mongoose's body size is relatively small compared to other objects in the picture.
Many mongoose species exhibit a characteristic standing posture with the aid of their tail where they stand on their hind legs to survey their surroundings.
Mongooses are known for their agility and quickness. They are often seen darting and weaving to avoid predators.
meerkat: Meerkats have a thin, tapered body with a pointed snout, distinguishing them from other animals.
They typically have a coat with light gray to brown fur, often with stripes that run in parallel from the base of the tail to the shoulders.
They have prominent, rotating ears which are nearly hairless and a distinct dark patch around their eyes.

They are typically shown in a standing posture on their hind legs, using their tail for balance, and scanning the surroundings. This is very characteristic of their behavior and helps identify them in images.
Meerkats have thin, pointed tails which often measures about 7-10 inches, about the same length as their bodies.
They have long, sharp non-retractable claws that they use for digging. These claws can often be seen in close-up images.
They are often found in groups, as meerkats are highly social animals. This can help in identifying them in images where more than one animal is present.
tiger beetle: Tiger beetles are notably characterized by their long, slender body with a hard, shiny exoskeleton that can range in colors from metallic green to coppery brown.
They are known for their large, bulging eyes and six long legs, which allow them to be fast and agile runners.
The relative size of tiger beetles can be smaller compared to other objects in the image.
Tiger beetles have unique, sickle-shaped mandibles that make them efficient and voracious predators.
They possess antennae that are about half as long as their body and are positioned between their eyes and the mandibles.
The elytra or wing covers of the tiger beetle often have white or yellow markings, and the pattern of these markings can help in differentiating the different species.
When observed in a profile, they have a noticeable humpbacked shape.
ladybug: Ladybugs are typically small and oval-shaped or hemispherical insects.
Ladybugs are well known for their iconic red and black spotted coloration, but they can also come in other colors like yellow, orange, black, and even pink.
The size of ladybugs is smaller compared to other objects in the image, usually ranging from 1 to 10 millimeters in length.
Ladybugs have six short legs that are black in color.
Ladybugs have two sets of wings. The pair visible when they are not flying are hardened and often brightly colored with distinctive spots.
When disturbed, ladybugs can retract their legs and play dead.
Some species of ladybugs have stripes instead of spots.
ground beetle: Ground beetles are a large, cosmopolitan family of beetles, Carabidae, with more than 40,000 species worldwide, approximately 2,000 of which are found in North America and 2,700 in Europe.
They are typically black, but can exhibit metallic hues and are usually characterized by their shiny appearance.
Ground beetles are usually flat and elongated or rounded. About an inch long.
Other colorations are green, copper, blue, or a combination, often metallic.
Ground beetles have powerful mandibles that are pointed forward from their head that are used for cheving up their prey.
Their eyes are directly on the side of the head, and their are two antennae that are a bit longer than their body.

Some kinds of ground beetles, especially those of the genus Carabus and of the subfamily Cicindelinae (Tiger Beetles), are known to have a highly developed set of eyes that distinctly bulge from the sides which are used to spot their prey from afar.
longhorn beetle: Longhorn beetles are characterized by their exceptionally long antennae, which can be as long as or longer than the beetle's body.
Longhorn beetles have large, robust bodies, varying widely in size and color. They can be seen in various tones of brown, black, red or even metallic.
Most longhorn beetles have elongated and cylindrical bodies, which contributes to their name.
The wings of the longhorn beetles are known as elytra, covering the second pair of functional wings and the abdomen when at rest.
Longhorn beetles have strong mandibles, which they use for gnawing and eating.
Longhorn beetles have compound eyes which are usually notched at the base of the antennae.
Some longhorn beetle species have distinctive markings or patterns on their bodies and elytra, making them more recognizable.
leaf beetle: Leaf beetles come in a variety of vibrant colors, from metallic blue, green, and gold to more subdued shades of brown or black.
Leaf beetles are characterized by their oval or roundish compact bodies, which range in size from small to medium.

Alpine ibex: The Alpine ibex, also known as the steinbock or bouquetin, is a species of wild goat known for its muscular build and sturdy physique.

The Alpine ibex is characterized by its short, dense coat which is primarily brownish to grey in color. In the winter, the coat is darker and longer.
