The steering wheel on a go-kart is typically in the center of the kart, with the gas and brake controls mounted to the sides.
Go-karts often have large, visible tires with deep treads for off-road use, or slick, smooth tires for track racing.
golf ball: Golf balls are usually white, but can also be found in other high visibility colors such as yellow and pink.
They tends to be small round objects in the frame, typically with a diameter of 1.68 inches.
Golf balls are characterized by their dimpled surface, designed to reduce aerodynamic drag and optimize flight characteristics.
They are usually found on the golf course or in the golf-related environment, which might help us identify them.
Golf balls are typically made of durable cover materials, like urethane, and may sometimes appear shiny or glossy in images depending on lighting conditions.
They can also be seen with branding or numbering marks on them.
Golf balls might be seen in proximity to golf clubs in images.
golf cart: Golf carts are small vehicles usually designed with two rows of seating that can accommodate up to four persons.
They often come in designs with three or four wheels and have a canopy on top.
Golf carts are slow-moving vehicles, capable of speeds usually up to 15 miles per hour.
They are normally used within golf courses for the transportation of players and their equipment.
They are powered either by electric motors or gasoline engines.
Golf carts often feature a small cargo bed at the back for carrying golf clubs and other equipment.
Depending on the model, they might have features like windshields, headlights, and indicator lights.
gondola: Gondolas are flat-bottomed, traditional Venetian rowing boats, often associated with the waterways of Venice, Italy.
They are long, sleek and typically painted black, as per an ancient Venetian law.
They are commonly maneuvered with the use of a single oar which is handled by a gondolier.
The front end of a gondola often rises higher than the rear, a unique feature known as its 'ferro' or iron.
Characteristically, gondolas have a covered cabin, or 'felze', for passengers in the middle, while the gondolier stands behind to row and navigate.
They typically carry two to six passengers, represented by the number of seats visible.
Gondolas are usually found in calm and shallow waters, like lagoons and canals.
gong: Gongs are usually round, flat, metal discs, with a turned edge.
The color of gongs is usually bronze or brass, but it can also be silver, depending on the material used to create it.
Gongs vary in size, from small handheld models to large, extremely resonant varieties used in orchestras.
Gongs can have a centrally located boss, or raised section, or can be completely flat.
They are traditionally struck with a padded mallet, which can often be seen in the image next to the gong.
Gongs often have a distinctive, bright, shimmering sound when struck, although this sound cannot be captured visually.
They're often associated with Asian cultures and can be found in traditional music, ceremonies, and rituals.
gown: Gowns are typically a type of long flowing dress usually worn in formal occasions by women.
The neckline and sleeve styles of gowns can range from strapless, sleeveless, spaghetti straps, to halter neck, etc.
Gowns often have a fitted bodice with a loose, elegantly draped skirt that reaches the ankles or floor.
Many gowns have elaborate details such as beading, sequin embellishments, or lace appliques.
The fabrics used in gowns range from satin, silk, lace, tulle, chiffon and organza.
Gowns can be found in many colors like black, white, red, blue, gold, silver, and pastels.
Gowns often come with a coordinated accessory like a scarf, bolero jacket or shrug to provide modest coverage.
grand piano: Grand pianos are known for their elegant, curved shape, with a long, flat top that can be lifted to expose the strings and soundboard.
Grand pianos are typically black, brown, or white, and made of polished wood or shiny lacquer finish.
The keyboard of a grand piano consists of 88 keys, both white and black, with the white keys for the seven major musical notes and the black keys for the intermediate notes.
The interior of a grand piano reveals a large cast iron harp or plate that holds numerous tightly stretched strings.
The relative size of a grand piano is larger compared to other objects in the image.
The configuration of a grand piano is horizontal, with strings and soundboard lying flat and extending away from the keyboard.
Most grand pianos have three pedals, including the soft pedal (una corda), sostenuto pedal, and sustain pedal (damper).
greenhouse: Greenhouses are usually made of transparent material such as glass or plastic, allowing sunlight to enter and warm the interior.
Greenhouses can come in various shapes but are typically rectangular or circular structures with peaked or domed roofs.
The interior of a greenhouse is often filled with plants, either on the floor or on shelving units. The relative size of a greenhouse is often larger compared to other objects in the image.
The greenhouses often have forms of ventilation, visible as openable panels or windows on the side or top of the structure.
Greenhouses might be seen in rural or suburban settings, often in the vicinity of a main residential or commercial building.
Frame materials of greenhouses can vary; some are metal or wooden while other high-end versions can have a steel frame.
Greenhouses sometimes have equipment like fans, heaters, and drip irrigation hoses to create a controlled environment for plants.
radiator grille: Radiator grilles are typically found at the front of a vehicle, providing air flow to the radiator to cool the engine.
They often have a characteristic pattern or design, which is integral to the brand identity of the vehicle manufacturer.
The material of radiator grilles can vary but is often made of plastic, aluminum, or stainless steel.
The color would typically match with the entire aesthetics of the vehicle, often in shades of chrome, black or body color.
Grill shapes can vary greatly, ranging from horizontal or vertical bars to honeycomb or mesh designs.
Some radiator grilles are integrated with the front bumper, others are separate components.
In many vehicles, the brand's logo or emblem is prominently displayed on the radiator grille.
grocery store: Grocery stores are known for their long aisles filled with various products, such as food, beverages, household goods, and more.
Grocery stores usually have areas for fresh produce, including fruits and vegetables, often placed in display bins or on shelving.
They typically have a bakery and deli section where fresh bread, meats, and cheeses can be purchased.
Grocery stores may have a frozen section with refrigerators or freezers for storing frozen foods like ice cream, frozen vegetables, and frozen meals.
They usually feature check-out counters or self-service kiosks at the front of the store where customers pay for their purchases.
Grocery stores may also have sections for non-food items, such as cleaning supplies, personal care products, and pet products.
Smaller convenience-based grocery stores may have less variety and lower quantities of products, but larger supermarkets or hypermarkets often have wide varieties and ample stock.
guillotine: The guillotine is a tall structure, often made of wood, with a sharp blade suspended at the top.
The blade of the guillotine is heavy, flat and angled, designed for quick descent and a clean cut.
There is an opening at the bottom of the structure where the neck of the person to be executed would go.
Guillotine is associated with the French Revolution, where it was used as a means of execution.
It typically has a rope or cord which, when released, allows the blade to drop.
The distinct shape of the structure with two upright posts connected by a crossbeam is very recognizable.
The scale of a guillotine is large, usually towering over human figures in images.
hair clip: Hair clips are typically smaller in size compared to other objects in the image and are used to hold hair in place.
Hair clips can be made from a variety of materials, including metal, plastic, and fabric.
Depending on their design, hair clips can have a variety of shapes, such as rectangular, circular, or shaped like flowers, bows, or animals.
Hair clips often have a clasping or pin-like mechanism that allows them to hold the hair in place.
Some hair clips are adorned with decorative elements, like beads, rhinestones, or sequins, to add a stylish or cute appearance.
Hair clips can vary in color, with common colors being black, brown, and metallic shades, but they can also be colorful or multicolored.
Certain types of hair clips, like barrettes or snap clips, have a distinctive mechanism that allows them to be opened and closed.
hair spray: Hair sprays are usually contained in aerosol cans, which are cylindrical with a thin nozzle and a button on top.
The size of hair spray cans can vary, but they are usually small enough to be held in one hand.
Hair sprays are often made of metal or plastic. Metal cans often have a shiny surface, while plastic ones are often opaque or semi-transparent.
The design and color of the can often feature the logo or brand of the product. Some may also include visual descriptions or images of the effects it has on the hair.
Hair spray cans often have details about the product written on them, such as the brand name, the product name, its volume, instructions for use, ingredients, and other information.
Hair sprays can come in a variety of types according to their function, such as holding hair styles, providing shine, or protecting hair from heat.
When the button on top of the aerosol can is pressed, hair spray is released as a mist.
half-track: Half-tracks are vehicles with regular wheels at the front for steering, and caterpillar tracks at back to propel the vehicle and bear most of the load.
They are typically designed for military use as armored personnel carriers, command vehicles, anti-aircraft, or as an artillery tractor.
Recognized by their distinctive front wheels combined with rear tracks that replace the traditional rear wheels.
Half-tracks often have a robust construction to withstand rough terrains and hostile combat situations.
The size of a half-track is relatively larger compared to other civilian vehicles.
They often have distinct features such as reinforced body, military insignia, or mounted weaponry.
The body of a half-track is often painted in drab military colors such as olive, khaki or camouflaged.
hammer: Hammers usually have a solid, heavy head made of metal, often steel or iron.
The head of a hammer is attached to a longer handle, typically made of wood or metal.
One side of a hammer head is flat used for striking, while the other side can vary depending on the type of hammer. In the case of a claw hammer, it has a curved, fork-like shape for removing nails.
The size of hammers can vary, but they are generally compact enough to be manually handled.
The handle is often designed to be easily gripped, and may have a rubber or wrapped finish to improve grip and reduce slip.
There are multiple types of hammers which include sledgehammers, mallets, ball-peen hammers, and framing hammers, each with unique features and shapes.
Some hammers, such as the ball-peen hammer, have rounded ends for shaping metal.
hamper: Hampers are typically large basket-like containers, often made of wicker, plastic or cloth.
Hinged lids or covers are common features in most hamper designs, designed to conceal contents and keep them in place.
Depending on the design, some hampers have handles on the sides for easy transport.
Some hampers come with a cloth liner or bag to prevent smaller items from falling through the gaps in the basket weave.
Large hampers may have wheels or rollers at the bottom for increased mobility.
Hampers are often used for storage or organization, commonly for laundry or for food during picnics.
Hampers can vary in size, but are usually large enough to hold a substantial amount of items.
hair dryer: Hair dryers are generally handheld devices with a pistol-grip handle.
The main body of a hair dryer usually contains a heating element and a fan to push out the hot air.
They often have a nozzle on the front to direct the airflow.
Most hair dryers come with an additional shaped piece that can be attached to the nozzle to further focus the airflow, often used for styling.
The handle generally has buttons or switches for the adjustment of heat and airflow settings.
Hair dryers are usually made from hard, durable plastic materials.
There is often a cord attached to the base of the handle for supplying power.
hand-held computer: They are compact and small enough to hold in one hand, which makes them portable and easy to use on the go.
These devices often feature a touchscreen interface, but some models may also include physical buttons or a small keyboard for input.
They typically have a rechargeable battery and may also feature a power port for charging.
Many hand-held computers come with built-in wireless connectivity options, such as Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, and may also include GPS capabilities.
These computers often include a range of pre-installed software applications, including email and web browsers, and users can typically install additional apps based on their individual needs.
The operating system of a hand-held computer is usually a variant of a desktop system, specifically designed for mobile use. Common choices include iOS, Android, or Windows.
These devices often include built-in cameras, both front and back facing, for pictures and video calls.
handkerchief: Handkerchiefs are typically small and square-shaped, made of thin and soft fabric like cotton, silk, or linen.
The edges of handkerchiefs are often hemmed for durability and to prevent fraying.
Handkerchiefs can be various colors but are frequently seen in white, possibly with stripe or check patterns.
Some handkerchiefs may have decorative patterns, monograms, or embroidery on them for aesthetic appeal or to denote personal ownership.
Handkerchiefs can be seen folded in various ways, often into triangles or squares, or sometimes crumpled if in use.
Handkerchiefs might also be used as a pocket square, peeking out of the breast pocket of a suit jacket in a coordinated color or pattern.
In historical or formal contexts, you might see a lace-edged or intricately embroidered handkerchief, possibly perfumed
hard disk drive: Hard disk drives are rectangular, box-like devices, often black, silver or grey in color.
They are usually flat on their tops and bottoms, with one side having various electronic connectors for data and power connection.
Some hard disk drives can be identified by the presence of a circular metal plate visible on top, which is the actual disk inside the drive.
Most hard drives have a label on the top side with information like the manufacturer's name, model number, capacity, and other specifications.
They are generally larger than other computer components, including SSDs, but are significantly smaller than most other electronic devices.
Some hard disk drives are designed for desktop computers, and are larger. Others are designed for laptops, and are smaller.
Depending on the design and model, the top of a hard disk drive can be either smooth or have a slight protrusion in the middle.
harmonica: Harmonicas are small rectangular wind instruments that fit in the palm of a hand.
Harmonicas are characterized by a row of air holes, typically ranging from 10 to 24 holes, depending upon the type and complexity of the harmonica.
They are generally made from metal, wood, or plastic materials and can be various colors though metallic silver or black are common.
They often have a branded or decorative mark, indicating the note layout and key of the harmonica, usually located on the upper surface of the harmonica.
The harmonica is a free-reed instrument, meaning that it produces sound as air flows past a vibrating reed in a frame. This gives the harmonica its signature sound.
Some harmonicas, called chromatic harmonicas, include a slide button on the end to shift the pitch of the notes, adding versatility to the instrument.
The harmonica is commonly used in blues, folk, jazz, country, rock and roll, and pop music genres.
harp: The number of strings varies from 10 to 47 strings depending on the type of harp.
The strings can be made of gut, nylon or metal.
combine harvester: Combine harvesters are large farming implements with wide fronts, often containing rotating blades or reels.
They are predominantly used for the harvesting of grains, and could be seen in large agricultural fields.
A key feature is its long, metal arm system, where the harvested crop is expelled.
Combine harvesters are usually very large, typically the largest machines in a field setting, and often covering a significant portion of the image due to its size.
The machine's front, or 'header', can be wide and flat for crops like wheat or round and barrel-shaped for crops like corn.
Many combine harvesters are painted in bright colors, such as red or green, making it stand out in the field.
They have large, heavy-duty tires or tracks designed for field work.
hatchet: A hatchet is a small axe with a short handle used for chopping.
The head of a hatchet is typically made of high quality, hardened steel, and it might be seen as shiny and metallic in the image.
The handle of a hatchet is usually made up of wood or some sort of synthetic material.
One side of the hatchet head is flat and sharp-edged for splitting or hewing, while the other side can have a hammer-like shape.
The hatchet handle is usually short, around one to two feet long, for one-handed use.
The size ratio between the hatchet handle and head is typically quite certain, with the handle multiple times longer than the head.
The shape of the hatchet head is not varied significantly, usually a slightly curved blade meeting a flat top.
holster: The holster is a device used to hold or restrict the undesired movement of a handheld item, most commonly a handgun.
Holsters are often attached to a belt or waistband, but they can also be attached to other locations of the body, such as the ankle or chest.
They are typically made from materials like leather, nylon, or sometimes synthetic fabrics.
The design of holsters varies. Some are open or have a strap over the weapon for quick access, while others are concealed carry holsters meant to hide the weapon from view.
There are custom holsters designed to fit a particular handgun model, ensuring a tight fit and secure hold.
Some holsters are designed with extra pouches or compartments for carrying ammunition or other items.
Shoulder holsters usually have a harness system to distribute the weight of the weapon across the body.
home theater: Home theaters often consist of a large flat-screen television or projector as the focal point for viewing content.
Accompanying the viewing screen are multiple speakers positioned strategically around the room to provide a surround-sound experience.
Home theaters often contain comfortable seating arranged in a manner that all seats have a clear, unobstructed view of the screen.
The overall lighting of home theaters is typically dimmer, providing a conducive environment for watching movies or playing games.
Home theaters can also contain DVD or Blu-ray players, gaming consoles, or other multimedia devices connected to the screen.
Some home theaters are equipped with soundproofing materials on the walls, floors, and ceilings to enhance the acoustic quality of the space.
Often there will be cinema-inspired decor, such as posters of popular movies, popcorn machine, movie recliners, or a ticket booth.
honeycomb: A honeycomb is a waxen structure made by honey bees that consists of numerous hexagonal cells.
Honeycombs usually appear in a group of many joined together, forming a flat surface or comb.
The color of a honeycomb can vary, but it is usually yellow or golden when freshly made. Over time, it may darken due to the bees' constant travel and honey aging.
Typically, honeycombs are filled with honey which gives it a shiny, sticky appearance.
Cells in a honeycomb are six-sided or hexagonal in shape, signifying the geometric precision by which bees construct their combs.
Honeycombs can often be seen with bees on and around it as they play an integral role in its creation and the honey production process.
Depending on the age and use, some cells in the honeycomb might be capped with wax. These are typically cells that contain maturing honey stores or developing bee larvae.
hook: Hooks are typically made of metal, but can also be made of materials such as plastic or wood.
A key feature of hooks is their curved or angular shape, which is used to catch, hold, or pull objects.
They come in various sizes, from small hooks used in fishing to large hooks used in industrial applications.
Some hooks have a sharp point or barb at the end to prevent the object from easily slipping off.
Certain hooks, like grappling hooks or wall hooks, may have multiple prongs or points.
Hooks used for specific purposes, such as fish hooks or crochet hooks, have unique characteristics related to their function.
Some hooks, like coat hooks or command hooks, are designed to be mounted on walls or other surfaces.
hoop skirt: Hoop skirts are known for their bell-like shape, created by concentric rings or 'hoops' encased within the fabric.
Hoop skirts are usually full length, extending from the waist to the ankles.
The hoops inside the skirt made from materials like steel, plastic or cane, help to hold out the skirt's shape.
These skirts are often worn as part of historical costumes or formal wear, such as wedding dresses and ball gowns.
Hoop skirts may often appear in conjunction with other garments like corsets, petticoats, or bustles to achieve a specific silhouette.
Hoop skirts can appear cumbersome or exaggerated in size due to their unique structure.
The material of the hoop skirt can be varied, including silk, satin or cotton, and could have decorative elements like lace, bows, or ribbons.
gymnastic horizontal bar: It is an apparatus made of metal or fibreglass rods, commonly used in gymnastics performances.
The bar itself is smooth and cylindrical, usually with a diameter of around 2.8 centimeters.
The horizontal bar is typically set at a height that allows the gymnast to swing and perform stunts, normally standing at around 2.8 meters high.
The horizontal bar is usually set parallel to the ground.
A gymnast performing on the bar may be seen executing various flips and twists in mid-air.
Gymnasts grip the bar with chalk-covered hands to prevent slipping.
The area around the bar is typically clear to provide a safe landing zone for the gymnast.
horse-drawn vehicle: This type of vehicle is usually characterized by a large cart or carriage being pulled by one or more horses.
The vehicle is often designed in a vintage or historical style, reminiscent of the eras before motorized transportation.
Common types include carriages, buggies, wagons, or stagecoaches, each varying in size, style, and number of seats.
Horses hitched to the vehicle are typically equipped with specialized harnesses and bridles, designed for heavy pulling.
An essential part of the horse-drawn vehicle is the yoke or the bar that connects the horse to the vehicle.
Depending on the type of vehicle, it can have two or four large, spoked wheels.
Many horse-drawn vehicles have a driver's seat at the front, from where the horse or horses can be controlled.
hourglass: Hourglasses are often recognized by their iconic shape, with two glass bulbs connected by a thin neck through which sand flows.
Hourglasses are characterized by the presence of fine sand, usually white or golden, contained within the bulbs.
In contrast to many objects, the upper chamber of an hourglass is usually empty or partially filled with sand, while the lower chamber accumulates the sand over time.
The size of an hourglass can vary, but they are typically handheld and easily distinguishable from other objects in an image due to their unique shape.
The hourglass is usually symmetrical, meaning the top and bottom halves look alike save for the amount of sand in each chamber.
Hourglasses are typically poised upright, with the sand flowing downwards from the top bulb to the bottom bulb.
The sand inside an hourglass is intended to measure the passage of time, usually set to a specific duration, commonly one hour.
iPod: iPods come in a variety of color options, ranging from classic white and black to vibrant colors like blue, pink, and gold in later models.
Depending on the model, iPods have different body shapes and sizes, ranging from the small and square iPod Nano to the original rectangular iPod Classic.
iPods typically feature a single screen on the front, used for displaying menus, album art, and other information.
One of the most distinctive features of early iPod models is the click wheel, used for scrolling through options and selecting songs. Later models like the iPod Touch replace this with a touchscreen.
On the back of many iPods is a mirror-like polished metal surface, sometimes engraved with the iPod logo and other information.
Many iPod models have a headphone jack for connecting earphones, as well as a charging port on the bottom.
The iPod Touch models feature a built-in camera on the front and back.
clothes iron: Clothes irons are typically made from hard, durable materials like stainless steel or ceramic and are often rectangular in shape.
Many clothes irons have a pointed tip on one end, aiding in ironing hard-to-reach areas such as collars and between buttons.
Clothes irons commonly have a handle at the top for users to hold onto while ironing.
The bottom surface of a clothes iron, called the soleplate, is usually flat and smooth, allowing the iron to glide effortlessly across the fabric.
Most clothes irons have dials, buttons, or digital displays on their body to control temperature and steam levels.
Clothes irons use heat and steam to remove wrinkles from fabrics. When in use, steam may be seen emitting from the iron.
In many designs, a clothes iron will have a cord attached to it, used for connecting to a power supply.
carved pumpkin: A carved pumpkin, also known as a jack-o'-lantern, is identified by the hollowed interior and cut-out designs, often a face, on its surface.
The color of a carved pumpkin is usually orange, but can also vary in shades of yellow or white depending on the variety of the pumpkin.
A key identifying feature is the presence of a lid or a cut-out top, which is removed to allow access for scooping out the pumpkin's interior.
The cuts and designs of a carved pumpkin are often illuminated from within, typically by a candle or a light, providing a glowing effect especially in low-light conditions.
There could be varying levels of complexity in the carved design from simple triangle cut-outs for eyes and jagged mouth to highly intricate designs.
A carved pumpkin can vary in size, commonly ranging from small table-top displays to larger ones placed at doorsteps or yards.
Most carved pumpkins are relatively even in shape, with a flat base for stability, but surface texture can vary from smooth to deeply ridged.
jeans: Jeans are typically made out of denim or dungaree cloth, which can be identified by their rugged texture and unique twill weaving pattern.
Jeans are typically blue or black, although they come in a variety of other colors and washes.
Jeans have distinctive stitching, often in a contrasting color to the denim. This might be particularly noticeable on the pockets and the side seams.
Jeans usually have a zipper or button front closure and are designed to be fitted on the waist.
Jeans often have five pockets: two back pockets, two front pockets, and a small watch or coin pocket inside one of the front pockets.
The fit of jeans can vary widely, from skinny and straight cuts to wide, flared, or bootcut styles.
Jeans may have particular features like rips, tears, patches, or embellishments as part of their design.
jeep: Jeeps are often associated with a rugged, boxy design and are known for their superior off-road capabilities.
Jeeps often have a prominent seven slotted front grill which is very iconic to the brand.
Most jeeps feature high ground clearance, providing better visibility and enabling it to traverse rocky or uneven terrain.
Jeeps often have large, heavy-duty tires suitable for off-road driving.
Many models come with a removable top and doors, allowing for a convertible-like, open-air experience.
The jeep logo or branding is often visible in one or more locations on the vehicle, such as the front, back, or sides.
Jeeps often have round headlights and square tail lights.
T-shirt: T-shirts typically have a simple, unisex design with a round neck and short sleeves. They can also come in a V-neck variant.
Most T-shirts are made of a lightweight, breathable fabric like cotton or polyester.
They often come in solid colors, but can also have patterns, graphics, or text printed on them.
T-shirts are typically a pullover garment, with no buttons or zippers.
The relative size of T-shirts varies based on the size of the wearer but generally, it should appear smaller than a person's upper body in the image.
Depending on the design, some T-shirts may have a pocket on the chest area.
T-shirts are usually more form fitting around the torso, but can also come in a loose, relaxed fit.
jigsaw puzzle: Jigsaw puzzles are usually made up of many small, interlocking and tessellating pieces. Each piece usually has a small part of a picture on it.
When complete, a puzzle produces a complete picture. This picture can be a wide variety of images such as scenic landscapes, famous artworks, or repeating patterns.
The edges of jigsaw puzzle pieces are uniquely cut, designed to fit perfectly with other pieces.
Each piece of the puzzle is different and has its unique shape, which helps to form the picture.
Puzzle pieces may vary in complexity, some having more tabs and blanks (interlocking parts) than others.
Jigsaw puzzles come in a range of sizes, with larger puzzles often being more complicated and containing a greater number of pieces.
Some jigsaw puzzles may have pieces that are all one color, or pieces that are different colors depending on the image the puzzle forms when complete.
rickshaw: Rickshaws are typically three-wheeled vehicles with a covered area for passengers in the back.
Rickshaws are usually manually powered by a person, typically the driver, but they can also be motorized.
Rickshaws usually appear smaller in size compared to other street vehicles like cars, buses, and trucks.
They are commonly seen in Asia, particularly in densely populated urban areas.
The structure of the vehicle comprises a driver's seat in front with a passenger seating area at the back, often with a canopy or roof for weather protection.
Rickshaws have large-spoked wheels, typically at least two at the back and one at the front.
Depending on the region, the design, color, and adornment of rickshaws can vary significantly.
joystick: Joysticks are input devices commonly used in video gaming, known for their distinctive stick that pivots on a base and reports its angle or direction to the device it controls.
It typically has one or more push-buttons, used for various functions like shooting or jumping in video games.
They have a rounded top for easy gripping, and some even come with padded or textured surfaces for additional comfort.
The base of a joystick is often heavily weighted, to increase stability during use.
Some joysticks include additional features like vibration feedback, trackballs, or throttle controls.
They can come in both wired or wireless versions depending on the user's preference.
The relative size of a joystick is usually small compared to other objects in the image, enough to fit comfortably in the user's hand.
kimono: Kimonos are a traditional Japanese garment characterized by their straight seams, T-shape, and wide sleeves.
Konomos are typically made of silk, although they may also be made of other materials like cotton or synthetic fabrics.
They are often bright and colorful, featuring a variety of patterns which can range from simple geometric designs to complex scenes from nature or history.
Kimono patterns often have significant cultural or symbolic meaning, such as cherry blossoms for transience or cranes for longevity.
Kimonos are worn with a wide sash called an obi, which is tied in the back. The style and color of the obi can often indicate the formality of the occasion.
The way a kimono is worn and tied can provide information about the wearer, such as their marital status or level of formality.
Kimonos for women are typically more elaborate and brightly colored, while kimonos for men tend to be more restrained and in darker colors.
knee pad: Knee pads often come in pairs, designed to protect the front of the kneecaps from injury or discomfort.
Knee pads are typically made of tough outer materials to resist abrasion, and padded with foam or gel on the inner side for comfort.
Depending on their purpose, knee pads can have different designs. Some are round and flat to protect the knee from falls, while others have a hinged design to allow for more movement.
Knee pads are often paired with straps or sleeves that wrap around the back of the knee to keep them in place.
Knee pads designed for sports like volleyball or skateboarding might have an open back design to allow for better ventilation and flexibility.
Knee pads used in heavy duty applications like construction or gardening often have a hard plastic or metal outer shell to provide robust protection against sharp or hard objects.
Tactical knee pads used in military or law enforcement contexts could have additional features like quick-release buckles or camouflage patterns.
knot: Knots are used for fastening or tying two things together. They are usually made from thread, cord, string, or rope.
There are numerous kinds of knots, each with unique shapes and uses. Some common types include the Bowline knot, Square knot, and Slip knot.
Knots can be characterized by the interlocking pattern of the rope, cord, or string.
The tightness of a knot can vary depending on its use, with some knots being tightly bound while others are loose for easy adjustment or release.
The complexity of a knot can range from simple overhand knots to intricate decorative knots or complex sailing knots.
The size of the knot usually depends on the thickness and length of the rope, string or cord used.
Knots can be functional, used in sailing, climbing, and construction, or decorative, such as those used in macrame and knot-tying art.
lab coat: Lab coats are typically white, but they can come in other colors like light blue or green in certain scenarios.
Lab coats are made of material that's designed to resist spills and splashes, such as cotton or a polyester-cotton blend.
Lab coats are uniquely designed with a straight collar and long sleeves to protect the wearer's skin.
Lab coats typically have buttons or snaps down the front for closure. Some designs include a back-belt for fit adjustment.

mailbox: Mailboxes are often found outdoors and are used for the deposit and retrieval of mail.

tights: Tights are a close-fitting garment, covering the body from the waist down, usually worn by women or girls.

Depending on their model and make, modems can have different types of status LEDs - typically representing power, broadband link, Internet, and Ethernet ports.
monastery: Monasteries are often large stone buildings with a serene and secluded setting, usually surrounded by nature.
They have distinctive architectural features such as high walls and towers, narrow windows, arched doorways, and podiums.
The architecture of monasteries can range from simple and austere to ornate and grand, depending on the particular religious order and time period.
They often include interior parts like a chapel or church, a refectory for dining, dormitories for the monks or nuns, cloisters, and often a library or scriptorium.
Monasteries are generally quiet, tranquil places, designed to promote contemplation and spiritual practice. This can sometimes be inferred from the characteristics of the surrounding environment.
Many monasteries have gardens or cultivated land, where the monks or nuns may grow their own food.
Some monasteries -- particularly those in Orthodox Christianity -- are painted with vibrant frescoes depicting scenes from the Bible or the lives of saints.
monitor: The monitor is the device that displays the video and graphics information generated by the computer through the video card.
Monitors are usually rectangular shaped and can come in a variety of sizes ranging from small screens to large displays.
It usually has a few buttons along the bottom or side edge, these are used to navigate its on-screen menu, adjust brightness and contrast.
The back of a monitor often has ports for HDMI, VGA, DVI or DisplayPort. This is where you connect the monitor to your computer.
Modern monitors are typically flat-panel displays utilizing LED or LCD technology, while older monitors use CRT technology.
Many monitors also have in-built speakers and may have a 3.5mm jack for headphone connection.
Some monitors are touchscreen, capable of receiving input from touches, swipes and other gestures.
moped: Mopeds are typically smaller than motorcycles, with a less powerful engine usually not exceeding 50cc.
Mopeds typically have a step-through frame design, allowing easy mounting and dismounting.
Mopeds usually have smaller wheels, typically around 10 inches in diameter.
Mopeds have a seat for the rider and often a second seat for a passenger, though they are not as comfortable for long distances as motorcycles.
They are typically equipped with pedals like a bicycle, which can be used for propulsion, starting the engine, or as a backup in case of engine failure.
Mopeds usually have automatic transmissions, making them easier to ride than motorcycles.
They are typically equipped with lights, mirrors, a horn, and a storage area for small items.
mortar and pestle: Mortar and pestle are typically made of hard materials, such as stone or hardwood, to resist wear from grinding.
Mortars are usually a round bowl shape, while pestles can vary between a rounded, club-like shape to a more cylindrical form.
The size of the mortar and pestle is relatively small compared to other kitchen utensils in the image.
They are used to crush and grind ingredients into a fine paste or powder, therefore remnants of spices or herbs can often be seen.
Mortar and pestle have a durable, solid feel, the weight of which aids in the grinding process.
They are usually found in kitchens, so a kitchen environment may be visible in the background of the photo.
The materials used to make mortar and pestle set are often marble, granite, or ceramic, each having a distinct texture and color.
graduation cap: Graduation caps, also known as mortarboards, are typically black and have a flat, square-shaped top.
The cap is usually worn as part of academic dress during graduation ceremonies and symbolizes the accomplishment of the graduate.
The cap commonly features a tassel, which hangs from the center of the board. The tassel is commonly worn on one side and then shifted to the other to symbolize commencement.
The tassel may come in different colors, often symbolizing the graduate's school or department.
The graduation cap, in the context of its surroundings, often stands out against a crowd during a ceremony due to its distinct shape.
The cap generally looks flat and rigid. However, some may feature customization or decorations.
The size of the cap relative to the student's head is typically snug or fitted.
mosque: Mosques typically have a distinctive architectural style, influenced by Islamic art and culture.
Many mosques have a tall, slim structure known as a minaret, from which calls to prayer are traditionally made.
The main dome of a mosque is often a notable feature, often decorated with intricate design and the crescent moon symbol, a widely recognized Islamic symbol.
Mosques often have a large entrance portal or iwan, which is usually arched and highly decorated.
Inside, a mosque will contain a mihrab, a niche in the wall that indicates the direction of Mecca, towards which Muslims pray.
Some mosques also have a minbar, a raised platform in the mosque from where the imam (leader) delivers sermons.
Walls inside mosques are often decorated with intricate geometric patterns and Arabic calligraphy, especially verses from the Quran.
mosquito net: Mosquito nets are typically white or light-colored and made of lightweight, mesh-like material that blocks mosquito entry.
Mosquito nets are constructed of a grid of tiny holes that are big enough to allow airflow but small enough to prevent mosquitoes from passing through.
Mosquito nets typically hang from a central point at the top and drape down around the bed or structure they're protecting.
Depending on their design, some mosquito nets hang freely while others are structurally supported to form a tent-like enclosure.
Mosquito nets used for travel or outdoor activities may be treated with insecticides or mosquito repellents to offer extra protection.
A properly installed mosquito net should not have gaps where mosquitoes can enter, and the bottom is typically tucked under the bed or sleeping mat.
In addition to their practical use, mosquito nets can often be found as decorative elements in tropical or fairytale-themed decor.
vespa: Vespas are recognized by their pressed, painted steel unibody which combines a complete cowling for the engine, a flat floorboard, and a prominent front fairing for wind protection.
Vespas are known for their unique design characterized by a high, rounded front shield, a large, comfortable seat, small diameter wheels, and a prominent single-sided front suspension.
Most Vespas have the logo placed on the front shield and unique badges on the sides.
The Vespa's engine is located on the right side of the vehicle, with the transmission directly connected to the wheel for drive.
Vespas use a manual transmission with the gear and clutch controls located on the left handlebar.
Vespa scooters have a signature step-through frame design, allowing the rider to mount and dismount without swinging a leg over the seat.
The rear part of a Vespa usually has a pillion seat which can also be used as a storage area.
mountain bike: Mountain bikes are typically heavier and more rugged than road bikes, designed for off-road cycling and unpaved terrains.
Mountain bikes feature wider, knobbly tires for improved grip, shock absorption and traction on loose surfaces.
Mountain bikes usually have suspension on the front (known as 'hardtail') or on both the front and rear (known as 'full suspension') to absorb impact from rough terrain.
The frame geometry of mountain bikes is typically more relaxed than road bikes, allowing riders to sit in a more upright position for better control and visibility.
Mountain bikes often have disk brakes - either mechanical or hydraulic - for effective stopping power on steep slopes and muddy or rocky conditions.
Mountain bikes frequently have flat or riser handlebars for more stability and control during downhill riding and technical manoeuvres.
Gearing on mountain bikes is typically lower to allow for efficient pedaling on steep and difficult climbs.
tent: Tents are portable shelters usually made of fabric and supported by poles.
Tents generally have a triangular shape to effectively shed rain.
Tents might vary in size, ranging from small ones that can only fit one person to large ones that can accommodate groups.
The tent's fabric exterior may come in a variety of colors, but common colors are green, blue, and brown.
Tents are often set up outdoors, particularly in camping, hiking, or festival settings.
Some tents have a rain fly, which is an additional waterproof cover placed over the top of the tent.
Many tents have a zippered entrance and some may have windows with mesh screens.
computer mouse: Computer mice commonly have a rounded, compact design to fit comfortably under the hand, but variations in design and shape exist across different models.
Typically, there are at least two buttons at the top of the mouse, separated by a scroll wheel in the middle.
The bottom surface of a mouse usually has a sensor (optical or laser) for tracking movement and small 'feet' to reduce friction with the surface the mouse is used on.
Majority of computer mice are predominantly black or white in color, but they come in a wide variety of colors and patterns depending on the brand and model.
The length and height of a typical mouse are smaller compared to other objects in the image.
Some models may feature additional buttons (like side buttons) for additional functionality.
A significant fraction of mice used today are wireless, but corded mice with a USB connector are also common.
mousetrap: Mousetraps are often rectangle-shaped, with a heavy, guillotine-like wire that snaps down when triggered.
A mousetrap traditionally has a wooden base, with a metal trip pedal and kill bar.
On most mousetraps, there is a bait cup or area where bait is placed to lure the mouse.
Some mousetraps are plastic and rectangular, with entry holes at either end allowing the mouse to enter.
Some modern mousetraps are electronic and box-shaped, killing the mice with an electric shock.
Many mousetraps have a small lever or trigger mechanism that releases when disturbed by a mouse, triggering the trap.
The relative size of a mousetrap is small and can be placed in corners, along walls, or where mouse activity is suspected.
moving van: Moving vans are often larger in size as compared to normal cars, due to their role in transporting goods, furniture, or other heavy items.
They are generally box-shaped vehicles to maximize storage space, and mostly painted white or in company color schemes.
They can frequently be identified by the presence of a company logo or other signage on the side or back of the vehicle.
Often, there are rear doors that swing open, or a large door that rolls up to allow for loading and unloading of items.
The vehicle may have a cab separate from the storage space, unlike regular passenger cars.
Some moving vans might be seen with a ramp or lift to assist in moving heavy items into the van.
The vehicle is typically devoid of external ornamentation or accessories, as function is prioritized over aesthetics.
muzzle: Muzzles refer to the part of an animal's face that includes the nose, mouth, and jaws, often prominent in dogs, horses and similar animals.
Muzzles can be long or short, broad or narrow, depending on the breed of the animal.
It may have fur, hair, or whiskers, and color varies based on the animal's overall coat color.
Some muzzles may be moist and black, characteristic of many dog breeds.
Muzzles may include notable features such as a split down the middle (like a dog's nose), large nostrils (like a horse), or sizable teeth (like a carnivorous beast).
Depending on the animal, the lower part of the muzzle may include features such as a pronounced chin and jowls.
The shape and length of a muzzle can vary greatly among dog breeds, from the short, squashed muzzle of a Bulldog to the elongated snout of a Greyhound.
metal nail: Metal nails are typically long and slender with a sharp tip on one end and a flat head on the other.
Nails are usually made from steel and have a shiny, metallic surface.
The relative size of a metal nail is significantly smaller compared to most objects in the image.
Nails are typically straight and have a uniform, cylindrical shape until the head.
Metal nails often have indents or lines on their head, designed for better grip with the hammer.
The length of nails can vary greatly, with small nails being a few centimeters long and larger ones several inches long.
Nails are typically seen in construction or DIY settings, like near wood, tools, or fastening objects together.
neck brace: A neck brace, also known as a cervical collar, is a medical device used to support a person's neck.
It is commonly made from plastic and foam, with soft pads for comfort. The outer plastic layer is rigid, providing the necessary support.
Neck braces are typically white or beige, although they can sometimes be found in other colors.
They are normally sized to fit snugly around the neck, covering the throat to the base of the skull and extending down almost to the shoulders.
Neck braces are secured with Velcro or similar fastening mechanisms, often in the back, so that they can be easily adjustable.
They are often used after surgical procedures or in the case of neck injuries to restrict movement and allow healing.
When worn, the brace limits the range of motion of the neck, preventing the wearer from turning or flexing to a significant degree.
necklace: Necklaces are typically made of a precious metal chain like gold, silver, or platinum.
Some necklaces come with pendants or charms, typically hanging from the center of the necklace, which can be of different shapes, sizes, and materials.
The length of necklaces varies, from short choker styles that wrap tightly around the neck to long opera length that hangs in the chest area or lower.
Necklaces may have a clasp or lock at the back which is generally smaller and less decorative, intended to secure the accessory around the wearer's neck.
Some necklaces are embedded with gemstones like diamonds, rubies, sapphires, emeralds, or less expensive stones like quartz, opal, or amber.
The style of necklaces can vary widely, from simple chain styles to complex, ornate designs with multiple layers or strands.
Some necklaces are personalized or custom-made, featuring initial letters, specific designs, or meaningful symbols.
baby pacifier: Baby pacifiers are small, often brightly colored, and made of a soft and flexible material.
It has a handle on one side for easy grip or attachment to clothing or toys.
The pacifier often has a shape that fits comfortably in a baby's mouth, with a rounded or bulb-like end where the baby sucks.
It usually has a ring or handle at the back, allowing a baby or parent to hold or remove it easily.
The pacifier will have a shield or guard that rests against the baby's lips to keep the baby from taking the pacifier too far into their mouth.
Pacifiers can come in a variety of colors and designs, sometimes featuring cute or playful images, such as animals or phrases.
Most pacifiers are made of baby-safe materials such as silicone, latex, or hard plastic.
notebook computer: Notebook computers have a clamshell design, with the display screen on one side and the keyboard on the other.
Notebook computers are portable and have smaller dimensions compared to desktop computers.
The keyboard layout of a notebook computer typically includes a QWERTY keyboard plus additional keys for functions, volume control, screen brightness, and others.
Notebook computers have a built-in display, which can vary in size and resolution. Some notebook computers may have touch screen capabilities.
On the periphery of the notebook computer, multiple ports can be seen such as USB, HDMI, SD card slot, and charging port.
Some notebook computers may have a separate numeric keypad on the right side of the keyboard, while others may integrate this into the main keyboard area.
Notebook computers typically have a touchpad below the keyboard for cursor control, although some may also have a pointing stick between the g and h keys.
obelisk: Obelisks are tall, narrow, four-sided structures, gradually tapering towards a pyramid shape at the top.
Obelisks are often made out of stone materials, such as granite or marble.
They are commonly found in significant historical sites and are associated with ancient Egyptian architecture.
Often the base of an obelisk is a square or rectangular shape with a pointed tip at the top.
Many obelisks have inscriptions, symbols, or hieroglyphs carved into their surfaces indicating their historical significance.
They are commonly found in public spaces like parks, commemorative sites, or in front of important buildings.
The relative size of an obelisk is larger compared to other objects in the image.
oboe: The oboe is a long, narrow woodwind instrument with a conical bore and flared bell.
It is typically made of black or dark brown wood, often Grenadilla or Rosewood, but there are also plastic versions available.
Oboes have a distinctive 'waistband' or metal band in the middle of the body, and a flared bell shape at the end.
The oboe is easily recognizable by its double reed mouthpiece, which is distinctly separate from the main body of the instrument.
The oboe has a series of keys running along its body which allow the player to alter the pitch of the notes produced by the instrument.
These keys are typically made of silver or nickel silver.
The sound produced by an oboe is distinct and can be identified as a clear, piercing, poignant, and personal tone.
ocarina: The ocarina is a small, portable wind instrument, usually made of ceramic, clay, metal, plastic, or wood.
It's often egg-shaped with holes on its surface for fingers to cover and uncover to produce sound.
The position and number of holes on the ocarina may vary, but traditional versions often have four to twelve holes.
It typically has a sweet, haunting, and ethereal sound which makes it easy to distinguish aurally from other wind instruments.
The size and shape of ocarinas can vary significantly, ranging from small, pendant-like designs to larger, more complex shapes.
Ocarinas can be found in different color and designs, typically based on the materials from which they are made.
Some ocarinas have unique designs like double or triple chambers for playing more complicated music.
odometer: Odometers are typically found in vehicles, particularly cars and motorcycles, and they track the total distance that the vehicle has traveled.
Traditional analog odometers display the distance traveled with rotating mechanical dials, with each dial representing a digit.
Modern digital odometers show the distance traveled on a digital display, often as part of a larger unit that includes other vehicle information.
Odometers usually display a series of digits, which represents the number of miles or kilometers that the vehicle has driven.
In images, odometers can often be seen behind the steering wheel or in the dashboard of the vehicle.
The number value on an odometer usually increases from left to right, with each dial or digit space representing a power of ten.
Odometer readings are often used to determine a vehicle's usage, with higher numbers indicating more extensive use.
oil filter: Oil filters are generally cylindrical in shape, resembling a small metal can or cup.
They usually have a metal body with a threaded hole at the center of one end, to be screwed into the engine's oil system.
Oil filters are usually identifiable by their size, often with a diameter of a few inches and a length that is slightly larger.
Oil filters come in a variety of colors, but they are often white, black or orange.
Many filters have brand-specific markings or labels, which can help in identification.
The inside of an oil filter generally contains a filtration material such as synthetic fibers or cellulose that is folded into pleats.
They are typically sealed with gaskets or rubber o-rings to ensure a tight fit.
pipe organ: Pipe organs are known for their large size, often taking up a large portion of the space within a church or concert hall.
The structure of pipe organs involve a series of pipes of varying lengths and widths, which produce different tones when air is blown through them.
Pipe organs often feature a complex array of keyboards, or manuals, which are played by the organist's hands, and a pedalboard played by the feet.
The console of the pipe organ, where the organist sits to play, contains several rows of keys and a variety of control switches, knobs, and pedals.
The facade of the pipe organ typically contains the largest and most decorative pipes, which are often painted or gilded.
Pipe organs are commonly found in churches, cathedrals, concert halls, and some schools and universities.
Details of the organ's design may vary, but many feature intricate, artistic carvings or decorations on the console and facade.
oscilloscope: An electronic instrument used to measure and display voltage signals over time. It is essential in electronics for analyzing waveforms and diagnosing circuits.
An oscilloscope is a type of electronic test instrument that graphically displays varying signal voltages.
Most oscilloscopes are box-shaped with a display screen on the front, together with various knobs and buttons for control.
On the display screen, waveforms (usually in a two-dimensional graph) can be seen, which represents the signal in either time or frequency domains.
Some oscilloscopes are equipped with several channels, indicated by multiple input connectors, each able to handle a separate signal for simultaneous observation.
Knobs and buttons on an oscilloscope usually include controls for focus, intensity, horizontal and vertical scaling, triggering, and channel selection.
Many modern oscilloscopes may also include digital functions, such as a USB port, and display features like grid lines to assist in signal measurement.
overskirt: An overskirt is a type of garment that is worn over another skirt, dress, or similar clothing item.
Overskirts often have a gathered or draped design, creating a layered effect over the base garment.
Depending on the design, an overskirt might cover just the front or back of the base garment, or it could encircle the entire waistline.
Overskirts come in a variety of materials, including fabrics like satin, tulle, lace, or velvet. The material of the overskirt may match or contrast with the base garment.
Some overskirts are attached to the waistband of the base garment and may have a closure like a zipper or buttons.
Besides plain styles, overskirts can feature details like ruffles, pleats, bows, or other decorative elements.
Overskirts are often worn for special occasions or formalwear, and may be seen in designs like ball gowns, wedding dresses, or other elaborate outfits.
bullock cart: Bullock carts are usually made of wood with two large, solid wheels.
It is typically drawn by one or two bullocks, which are large domesticated bovines.
The cart is connected to the bullocks by a yoke placed on their necks.
Features might display simple, rustic engineering often crafted from local materials.
The cart part usually has a flat surface, and some may have a canopy to protect users from the sun and rain.
The size of a bullock cart can be relatively large compared to other objects in an image, depending on the perspective.
Some bullock carts might be filled with produce, farming materials or sometimes people.
oxygen mask: It is a device placed over the nose and mouth that delivers pure oxygen from an attached supply.
The mask typically covers the nose and mouth, with a clear, plastic design, so the face is still visible.
There are straps that go around the back of the head to hold the mask securely in place.
The mask is connected to a tube that leads to an oxygen source like a portable oxygen tank or an oxygen concentrator.
The design can vary with some models covering the entire face, while others only cover the nose and mouth.
Many masks have vent holes or valves to ensure exhaled air can escape and to prevent carbon dioxide buildup.
Some models include a reservoir bag to store oxygen and supply it during inhalation.
product packet / packaging: Packaged products commonly have branding, including logos, taglines, or unique color schemes.
Packets and packages often contain information about the product, such as ingredients, instructions, and nutritional facts.
The shape and size of the package can vary depending on the product it contains.
Some packages use specific colors or imagery to denote certain kinds of products, like green for organic or images of fruit for flavored items.
Packages can be made from various materials, including plastic, metal, glass, or paper.
The package may have a specific opening mechanism, such as a screw cap, flip-top, pull tab, or tear strip.
Some packaging includes promotional messages or offers, such as 'new and improved', 'limited edition', or 'now with 25% more'.
paddle: Paddles are typically long, with a broad blade at one end used for propelling watercrafts like canoes or kayaks.
They are usually made of lightweight materials, like wood, plastic, or carbon fiber, to make them easy to use.
Paddles often have a T-shaped handle at the top, used to grip and control the paddling motion.
The blade of a paddle is often broad and flat, designed to push against the water and propel the boat forward.
Some paddles are double-bladed, with blades at both ends of the shaft, typically used for kayaking.
The length and size of paddles can vary depending on its intended use. Longer paddles are typically used for larger or tandem boats, while shorter ones are used for individual watercraft.
Paddles can come in various colors, though they are often in natural wood tones, bright colors, or have reflective elements for visibility.
paddle wheel: A large wheel with paddles used to propel boats or generate power. It is often associated with steamboats and watermills.
Paddle wheels are usually large, rotating wheels made up of a series of paddles or blades, specifically designed to propel water vehicles such as steamboats.
The paddle wheel is typically positioned at the stern or sides of the ship, with each 'paddle' dipping into the water to push the boat forward or backward.
Most paddle wheels have a circular frame with evenly spaced paddles around the circumference.
The paddles are flat and broad, allowing for maximum water displacement and propulsion.
Paddle wheels are usually made of metal or wood and are often painted, often in colors like red or black.
In operation, paddle wheels rotate, creating a distinctive splashing sound and visual display of water being pushed away.
padlock: Padlocks are small, portable locks that are commonly used for locking gates, sheds, lockers, or chests.
Padlocks typically have a U-shaped shackle that can be passed through an opening to prevent access or theft.
The body or casing of a padlock is often made of metal such as brass or steel, and can be rectangular, square, or round in shape.
Padlocks can be operated using a key or a combination mechanism. Key-operated padlocks have a keyhole, usually on the bottom.
Combination padlocks do not have a keyhole but instead have a series of rotating discs or dials that are used to set the lock combination.
The shackle of a padlock is typically made of strong, hard metal such as steel, which is resistant to cutting or sawing.
Some padlocks have a double-locking mechanism where the shackle enters the lock body at two points for extra security.
paintbrush: Paintbrushes typically have a handle, ferrule, and bristles and these could be identifiable features.
The bristles of the paintbrush could range from synthetic materials to animal hair, like hog or sable.
Depending on the type of paintbrush, the shape of the bristles could be flat, round, fan, or filbert.
The relative size might be smaller or comparably equal when placed beside objects like a palette or canvas.
Paintbrushes may often found with traces of paint on the bristles, across a spectrum of colors.
The handle of the paintbrush can vary in length - longer for canvas painting and shorter for detail work.
Paintbrush handles are typically made of wood and can come in various colors, although natural wood or black are common.
pajamas: Pajamas are usually soft, loose-fitting garments designed for sleeping or lounging at home.
Pajama sets often come in two-piece sets, typically consisting of a long-sleeve or short-sleeve top and matching bottoms.
Pajamas can come in a variety of materials such as cotton, silk, satin, or flannel.
The pattern or design on the pajamas can be quite distinctive, including things like solid colors, floral prints, animal prints, plaids, stripes, and cartoon characters.
Some pajamas may come with additional items like a matching robe, sleep mask, or slippers.
Pajamas can vary in length with long pajamas covering the whole leg, and short pajamas or shorts showing much of the legs.
Pajamas designed for colder climates or seasons may feature additional elements like a hood, footies, or thermal insulation.
palace: Palaces are often large and imposing structures, designed to impress with their size and grandeur.
The facades of palaces are often adorned with intricate architectural details such as sculptures, friezes, and carvings.
Palaces frequently have spacious courtyards and gardens, which can often be seen from the exterior.
Many palaces have distinctively shaped roofs or domes, which can often be a distinguishing feature of the architecture of the region.
The entrances to palaces are typically grand and ornate, often featuring large gates or archways.
Palaces are usually surrounded by high walls or fences for security.
Many palaces are painted or constructed in distinctive colors based on local cultural preference or available materials.
pan flute: Pan flutes are typically made of bamboo, reed, or other types of wood.
Pan flutes consist of multiple pipes, typically from 10 to 30, and each pipe produces a different note.
These pipes are arranged in a row, with each pipe being progressively larger (longer) than the one preceding it, giving the pan flute its distinctive shape.
Each pipe is closed at one end and open at the other. The player blows air into the open end to make a sound.
Pan flutes are often held horizontally when played, and the player moves their mouth across the different pipes to change the note being played.
In many designs, the pipes are secured together by a cord that runs through holes near the closed end of each pipe.
Despite the variety in the number of pipes and materials used, the basic shape and configuration of pan flutes is consistent and easily recognizable.
paper towel: Paper towels are usually available in the form of a roll with detachable sections.
These are typically white in color, but can be found in various other colors and patterns.
Paper towels have a soft, absorbent texture, making them ideal for soaking up liquids.
They are generally square or rectangular in shape and can be folded.
Paper towels can be one or two layers thick with an embossed or quilted pattern to enhance absorbency.
The relative size of paper towels is small compared to other objects in the picture, but larger than napkins or tissues.
Depending on the brand, paper towels can have perforations to make tearing off individual sheets easier.
parachute: Parachutes are typically large and round or oval when fully opened, taking on a concave shape.
They can come in a variety of colors, often with different segments of the parachute featuring different colors or patterns.
Parachutes are usually seen in the sky, often high above the land or sea, during daytime with clear or slightly cloudy skies.
Parachutes have suspension lines attaching the parachute canopy to the person or object it's slowing down.
In some instances, a person, known as a parachutist or skydiver, can be seen attached to the parachute. The parachutist is usually wearing a jumpsuit, helmet, and possibly goggles.
When a parachute is deployed, it may exhibit a rapid upward movement in the frame of the image due to the perspective from the ground.
Sport parachutes might have rectangular canopies due to steerable designs.
parallel bars: Parallel bars are long, straight, and narrow strokes. Each pair is arranged parallel to each other.
They are generally made of materials like steel, iron, or wood, with smooth surfaces.
Parallel bars are usually located in a gymnasium or indoor sports facility.
The bars are typically positioned at waist height and are adjustable to adapt to the height of the user.
The distance between the bars is also adjustable but it is usually set to be around the width of the user's shoulders.
They are commonly used for upper body exercises and body balancing, mainly in gymnastics.
Gymnasts use parallel bars to perform swinging, balancing, and strength-based techniques.
park bench: Park benches are typically made of wood, metal, or a combination of both.
The park bench is often found outdoors, in parks or public areas. The background might be trees, grass, or a walking path.
Park benches usually have a long, flat seating area, which can typically accommodate two or more people.
Park benches often have supports or armrests at each end, and some have a backrest while some do not.
The condition of park benches can vary greatly, ranging from newly installed and well-maintained to old, worn and occasionally vandalized.
Metal benches are usually painted, often a dark color or a green that blends well with grass and trees. Wooden benches may be painted or just varnished.
Benches might be found alongside paths, near playground or picnic areas, or in scenic spots with a good view.
parking meter: Parking meters are often metallic and either on a post or attached to a pedestal or wall.
They often have a digital or analog display showing the time left for parking.
Parking meters are found outdoors, often near the edge of sidewalks or in parking lots.
Parking meters usually have a coin slot or card reader for payment of the parking fee.
Some parking meters have a solar panel on top to power the electronic components.
Some parking meters are equipped with a functionality that allows payment via a mobile app.
They are often located in rows when in a car park or individually alongside the road where cars are parked.
railroad car: Railroad cars, also known as railway vehicles, are used for the transportation of both goods and passengers on rail tracks.
They are typically metallic and robust in structure to bear heavy loads and withstand long journeys.
Railroad cars come in various shapes and sizes, depending on their purpose. Some may be large and box-like for carrying goods, while others may have numerous windows for passenger transport.
Freight railroad cars may have sliding doors or open tops, depending on the nature of goods they carry. Passenger railroad cars, on the other hand, usually have doors at both ends.
The undercarriage of a railroad car features a set of four to eight wheels grouped in sets called 'trucks', connected to the rail tracks.
Many railroad cars have unique ID numbers or company logos on their exterior for identification purposes.
Railroad cars often have signal lights and safety signs as per transportation regulations.
patio: Patios are typically located directly outside of a house or apartment and are paved with materials such as stone, brick, tile or concrete.
Patios are often directly accessible from a home's interior, often through sliding glass doors or French doors.
Patios often include outdoor furniture such as tables, chairs, and loungers for dining or relaxation purposes.
A patio might come with additional features such as an outdoor fireplace, a grill, or a pergola.
Potted plants or other landscaping elements are often found on or around patios to enhance their aesthetic appeal.
Some patios may be covered by a roof or gazebo to provide shade and shelter from the elements.

picket fence: Picket fences are typically made of wood, but can also be seen in materials like vinyl and metal.

pickup truck: Pickup trucks are recognized by their large cargo area, known as the bed, which is open at the top and located at the back of the vehicle.

pier: Piers often extend over a body of water, usually the sea, a lake, or a river. They're built out from the shore.

piggy bank: Piggy banks are shaped like a pig, that comprises the body of the bank with a slot on top to drop coins in.

pill bottle: Pill bottles are generally cylindrical in shape and are typically made of plastic.

pillow: Pillows are often rectangular or square in shape, although they can also come in other forms such as round or even custom shapes.

ping-pong ball: Ping-pong balls are typically white or orange and have a matte finish.

pinwheel: Pinwheels are typically made of a stick with a windmill-like blade at the top that spins in the wind.

pirate ship: Pirate ships are typically wooden sailing ships from the late medieval period to the early 18th century.

drink pitcher: Drink pitchers are typically made from clear glass or plastic so the contents can be easily seen.

block plane: A block plane is a small woodworking hand plane which typically has the blade bedded at a lower angle than other planes.

planetarium: Planetariums are usually dome-shaped architecture that projects images of stars, planets, and other celestial objects onto their interior surface.

plastic bag: Plastic bags are often translucent or tinted in various colors and are made from thin, flexible plastic material.

plate rack: Plate racks are often used in kitchens for storing plates, bowls, and other dinnerware.

pole: Poles are long, skinny, and usually round objects that stand upright.

poncho: Ponchos are usually made from wool or other thick, warm materials suitable for weather protection.

soda bottle: Soda bottles often have a slim and elongated shape, often tapering towards the top.

plant pot: Plant pots are typically round or cylindrical in shape, but they may also be square or rectangular.

potter's wheel: Potter's wheels are circular and flat, designed to rotate around a central axis.

power drill: Power drills are generally handheld devices with a cylindrical shape.

prayer rug: Prayer rugs are usually rectangular and small enough to be easily portable.

printer: Printers are often made of hard plastic and come in varying sizes, usually in shades of white, black, or grey.

prison: Prisons are usually characterized by high walls with barbed wire or other security features on top to prevent inmates from escaping.

projector: Projectors typically have a box-like shape with a lens in the front from which the light is projected.

hockey puck: Hockey pucks are circular and flat, with parallel top and bottom surfaces.

punching bag: Punching bags can come in various shapes but are mainly cylindrical or teardrop-shaped and hung from the ceiling.

purse: Purses usually have various sizes and shapes but they are often designed to carry personal items and are usually not very large.

quill: Quills are the main flight feathers located on the wings and tail of a bird, typically larger in size.

One side of the quill shaft ends with a stiff, pointed tip, while the other side flares out into a series of soft, flat threads, known as barbs.
The barbs on a quill are arranged in a symmetrical pattern along the shaft, forming a vane that aids in the bird's flight.
Quills can come in a variety of colors, often matching the coloration of the bird they come from. They can be solid-colored or patterned.
Historically, quills were used as writing instruments when dipped in ink, due to their pointed tip and sturdy structure.

quilt: Quilts are typically composed of three layers: a top layer of pieced-together fabric, a middle layer of insulation or batting, and a bottom layer of backing material.

race car: Race cars often feature dynamic and aerodynamic shapes to improve speed and maneuverability.
